     1→# Plan: Self-Improving Agent Loop
     2→
     3→**Status:** Not Started
     4→**Priority:** High
     5→**Date:** 2026-04-20
     6→**Scope:** Close the three gaps that made Hermes Agent go viral — self-improving skills, agentic memory lifecycle, and the "$5 deployment" narrative — while preserving Moltis's stronger security and architecture foundations.
     7→
     8→## Context
     9→
    10→Hermes Agent reached 100k GitHub stars in 53 days. The viral hook is not a single feature but a product loop: the agent gets smarter with every interaction. Three concrete mechanisms drive this:
    11→
    12→1. **Self-improving skills** — after complex tasks, the agent autonomously creates reusable procedures
    13→2. **Agentic memory lifecycle** — memory isn't just a tool; it's a background process that extracts, prefetches, and evolves
    14→3. **"Runs anywhere for $5"** — SSH backend + serverless hibernation + one-command gateway setup
    15→
    16→Moltis already has stronger primitives than Hermes in most areas. What's missing is the **autonomous behavior loop** on top of those primitives.
    17→
    18→### Prior work
    19→
    20→- `plans/2026-03-28-plan-hermes-gap-roadmap.md` — broader roadmap (phases 0–5)
    21→- `plans/2026-04-10-plan-skills-native-read-tool.md` — `read_skill` tool (landed)
    22→- `crates/tools/src/skill_tools.rs` — `create_skill`, `update_skill`, `delete_skill`, `read_skill`, `write_skill_files` all exist
    23→- `crates/agents/src/silent_turn.rs` — pre-compaction memory flush already runs a hidden LLM turn
    24→- `crates/memory/` — FTS5 + vector embeddings, hybrid search, chunking, writer trait
    25→
    26→## Problem Statement
    27→
    28→Moltis has the tools for an agent to create skills and write memories, but **the agent never does so autonomously**. The create/update/delete skill tools exist, but the agent loop doesn't prompt or encourage their use. Memory writes only happen during the pre-compaction silent turn. There is no post-turn extraction, no prefetch, no session-end summary.
    29→
    30→Hermes solves this with three mechanisms Moltis lacks:
    31→
    32→1. **System prompt guidance** telling the agent to create skills after complex tasks
    33→2. **Memory lifecycle hooks** (pre-turn prefetch, post-turn sync, session-end summary)
    34→3. **Skill patching** — incremental fixes to skills the agent notices are stale or broken
    35→
    36→## Non-Goals
    37→
    38→- Copying Hermes's Python architecture or meta-tool patterns
    39→- Adding SSH/serverless backends (separate plan)
    40→- Building a skill hub or registry (separate plan, phase 4 in the roadmap)
    41→- Replacing Moltis's security model with convenience-first defaults
    42→- Adding new channels (separate effort)
    43→- Hermes-style RL or trajectory generation
    44→
    45→---
    46→
    47→## Part 1: Self-Improving Skills
    48→
    49→### What Hermes does
    50→
    51→In `agent/prompt_builder.py`, the system prompt includes:
    52→
    53→> "After completing a complex task (5+ tool calls), fixing a tricky error, or discovering a non-trivial workflow, save the approach as a skill with skill_manage so you can reuse it next time."
    54→
    55→The `skill_manager_tool.py` provides `create`, `edit`, `patch`, `delete`, and `write_file` actions. The `patch` action does surgical find/replace updates without rewriting the full skill. Created skills are scanned by `skills_guard.py` for dangerous patterns before activation.
    56→
    57→### What Moltis already has
    58→
    59→- `create_skill` tool — creates SKILL.md with frontmatter + body
    60→- `update_skill` tool — overwrites SKILL.md entirely
    61→- `delete_skill` tool — removes skill directory
    62→- `read_skill` tool — reads SKILL.md body + lists sidecar files
    63→- `write_skill_files` tool — writes sidecar files (references, templates, scripts, assets)
    64→- `moltis_skills::safety::scan_skill_body()` — injection pattern scanner (warn-only)
    65→- Checkpoint system — automatic pre-mutation snapshots
    66→
    67→### What's missing
    68→
    69→#### 1.1 System prompt guidance for autonomous skill creation
    70→
    71→**File:** `crates/skills/src/prompt_gen.rs` (or `crates/agents/src/prompt.rs`)
    72→
    73→Add a section to the system prompt, appended when skill tools are registered, that tells the agent:
    74→
    75→```
    76→## Skill Self-Improvement
    77→
    78→You have tools to create, read, update, and delete personal skills. Use them proactively:
    79→
    80→- After completing a complex task (5+ tool calls), consider saving the approach as a reusable skill with `create_skill`
    81→- After fixing a tricky error or discovering a non-obvious workflow, save it so you don't have to rediscover it
    82→- When a skill you're using has stale or incorrect instructions, update it with `update_skill`
    83→- When you notice a skill could benefit from reference data, use `write_skill_files` to add sidecar files
    84→
    85→Do NOT create skills for trivial or one-off tasks. Good skills encode multi-step procedures, domain-specific knowledge, or workflows that are likely to recur.
    86→```
    87→
    88→**Implementation:**
    89→- Add a `generate_skill_self_improvement_prompt()` function in `prompt_gen.rs`
    90→- Call it from the system prompt builder when `create_skill` is in the tool registry
    91→- Gate behind a config flag: `[skills] enable_self_improvement = true` (default true)
    92→- Add the config field to `crates/config/src/schema.rs` and update `build_schema_map()` in `validate.rs`
    93→
    94→**Tests:**
    95→- Unit test: prompt contains the guidance text when skill tools are enabled
    96→- Unit test: prompt omits the guidance text when `enable_self_improvement = false`
    97→
    98→#### 1.2 Skill patch tool (incremental updates)
    99→
   100→**File:** `crates/tools/src/skill_tools.rs`
   101→
   102→The current `update_skill` requires rewriting the entire SKILL.md body. Hermes has a `patch` action that does find/replace. This is important because:
   103→
   104→- The agent can fix a single line without re-generating the whole skill
   105→- Reduces hallucination risk (less content to generate)
   106→- Faster, cheaper (fewer tokens)
   107→
   108→Add a `PatchSkillTool`:
   109→
   110→```rust
   111→pub struct PatchSkillTool {
   112→    data_dir: PathBuf,
   113→    checkpoints: CheckpointManager,
   114→}
   115→
   116→// Tool name: "patch_skill"
   117→// Parameters:
   118→//   name: string (required)
   119→//   patches: array of { find: string, replace: string } (required, 1-10 items)
   120→//   description: string (optional — update the frontmatter description)
   121→```
   122→
   123→**Behavior:**
   124→1. Read current SKILL.md
   125→2. For each patch, do exact string replacement (fail if `find` not found)
   126→3. Optionally update frontmatter description
   127→4. Write back with checkpoint
   128→5. Run injection scan on the result
   129→
   130→**Tests:**
   131→- Happy path: single patch applied
   132→- Multiple patches in order
   133→- Patch not found → clear error
   134→- Traversal protection (same as other skill tools)
   135→- Injection scan runs on patched output
   136→
   137→#### 1.3 Post-task skill suggestion (agent loop hook)
   138→
   139→**File:** `crates/agents/src/runner/helpers.rs` (in `finish_agent_run`)
   140→
   141→After the agent loop completes, if:
   142→- The run used 5+ tool calls
   143→- The run was successful (no error)
   144→- Skill tools are available
   145→
   146→Then append a gentle nudge to the agent's final context:
   147→
   148→```
   149→[System note: This task used {N} tool calls. If the workflow you just completed is reusable, consider saving it as a skill with create_skill.]
   150→```
   151→
   152→This is **not** a forced action — it's a system-level hint that the agent can choose to act on or ignore. The agent still decides whether the task is worth saving.
   153→
   154→**Implementation:**
   155→- Add a `skill_creation_nudge` field to `AgentRunResult` (bool + tool call count)
   156→- In the gateway's post-run handling (where the response is sent back), if the nudge is set and the conversation is interactive, inject the note as a system message in the next turn
   157→- Gate behind `[skills] enable_self_improvement`
   158→
   159→**Alternative (simpler):** Instead of a post-run hook, just include the guidance in the system prompt (1.1 above) and trust the model to act on it. Hermes does it this way. Start with the simpler approach; add the post-run nudge only if models don't reliably self-improve with prompt-only guidance.
   160→
   161→**Decision:** Start with 1.1 (prompt-only). Revisit 1.3 if needed.

   164→
   165→## Part 2: Agentic Memory Lifecycle
   166→
   167→### What Hermes does
   168→
   169→Hermes's `MemoryManager` has lifecycle hooks:
   170→- `on_turn_start(query)` → prefetch relevant memories based on the user's message
   171→- `sync_all(user_content, assistant_content)` → after each turn, extract facts worth remembering
   172→- `on_session_end` → summarize the session's key learnings
   173→- `on_pre_compress` → save important context before compaction discards it
   174→- `queue_prefetch_all()` → background async prefetch for the next turn
   175→
   176→### What Moltis already has
   177→
   178→- `silent_turn.rs` — pre-compaction memory flush (runs an LLM turn to extract memories before compacting). This is equivalent to Hermes's `on_pre_compress`.
   179→- `memory_search` tool — agent can explicitly search memory
   180→- `memory_save` tool — agent can explicitly write memory
   181→- `memory_delete` tool — agent can remove memory entries
   182→- `MemoryWriter` trait — shared by save tool and silent turn
   183→- `MemoryRuntime` trait — search + sync operations
   184→- Hybrid search (FTS5 + vector) — better than Hermes's FTS5-only built-in
   185→
   186→### What's missing
   187→
   188→#### 2.1 Memory prefetch on turn start
   189→
   190→**Files:** `crates/chat/src/service/chat_impl.rs`, `crates/memory/src/runtime.rs`
   191→
   192→Before building the system prompt for each turn, query memory with the user's message as the search query. Inject relevant results into the system prompt as a `<recalled_context>` block.
   193→
   194→```rust
   195→// In the chat service, before calling the agent loop:
   196→if memory_enabled && !user_message.is_empty() {
   197→    let results = memory_runtime.search(&user_message_text, 3).await?;
   198→    if !results.is_empty() {
   199→        let recalled = format_recalled_context(&results);
   200→        system_prompt.push_str(&recalled);
   201→    }
   202→}
   203→```
   204→
   205→**Format:**
   206→```xml
   207→<recalled_context>
   208→The following was recalled from your long-term memory as potentially relevant:
   209→
   210→- [memory/2026-04-15.md] User prefers streaming API calls over batch...
   211→- [MEMORY.md] Project uses Rust workspace with 46+ crates...
   212→</recalled_context>
   213→```
   214→
   215→**Implementation details:**
   216→- Add `prefetch_memory(query: &str, limit: usize) -> Vec<SearchResult>` to `MemoryRuntime`
   217→- Call it in the chat service before prompt assembly
   218→- Gate behind `[memory] enable_prefetch = true` (default true)
   219→- Add config field to schema + validate
   220→- Use a low limit (3-5 results) to avoid prompt bloat
   221→- Skip prefetch for very short messages (< 10 chars) or system commands
   222→
   223→**Tests:**
   224→- Integration test: memory prefetch injects recalled context into prompt
   225→- Test: prefetch skipped when disabled
   226→- Test: prefetch skipped for very short messages
   227→- Test: empty memory returns no `<recalled_context>` block
   228→
   229→#### 2.2 Post-turn memory sync
   230→
   231→**Files:** `crates/chat/src/service/chat_impl.rs`, `crates/agents/src/silent_turn.rs`
   232→
   233→After each turn completes, run a lightweight background extraction. This is different from the pre-compaction flush — it runs after **every** turn, not just before compaction.
   234→
   235→**Design options:**
   236→
   237→**Option A: Background silent turn (heavier, more thorough)**
   238→- After each turn, spawn a background task that runs a mini silent turn
   239→- The mini turn reviews only the latest user message + assistant response (not the full history)
   240→- Writes to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` if it finds anything worth remembering
   241→- Pros: LLM-powered extraction is highest quality
   242→- Cons: doubles LLM cost per turn, adds latency if not truly async
   243→
   244→**Option B: Rule-based extraction (lighter, deterministic)**
   245→- After each turn, run heuristic extraction:
   246→  - If assistant mentioned a user preference → extract it
   247→  - If the turn resolved a technical issue → log the solution
   248→  - If the turn involved >N tool calls → log the workflow summary
   249→- Pros: zero extra LLM cost, instant
   250→- Cons: limited quality, hard to maintain rules
   251→
   252→**Option C: Periodic background flush (compromise)**
   253→- Every N turns (configurable, default 5), run a silent turn that reviews the last N turns
   254→- Between flushes, do nothing
   255→- Pros: amortizes LLM cost, still gets good extraction
   256→- Cons: can miss things if session ends before next flush
   257→
   258→**Recommendation:** Start with **Option C** (periodic flush every N turns). It's the best cost/quality tradeoff:
   259→
   260→```toml
   261→[memory]
   262→# Run a background memory extraction every N turns (0 = disabled, only pre-compaction)
   263→auto_extract_interval = 5
   264→```
   265→
   266→**Implementation:**
   267→- Add turn counter to chat service state
   268→- After each turn, increment counter
   269→- When counter hits threshold, spawn background silent turn with last N messages
   270→- Reset counter
   271→- Also flush on session end (new lifecycle event)
   272→
   273→**Tests:**
   274→- Unit test: counter increments and triggers at threshold
   275→- Unit test: counter resets after flush
   276→- Integration test: memories actually written after N turns
   277→
   278→#### 2.3 Session-end memory summary
   279→
   280→**File:** `crates/chat/src/service/chat_impl.rs`
   281→
   282→When a session ends (user closes chat, explicit `/end`, or timeout), run a final silent turn that:
   283→1. Summarizes what was accomplished
   284→2. Notes any unfinished work
   285→3. Saves to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`
   286→
   287→This ensures no conversation's context is lost, even if compaction never triggers.
   288→
   289→**Implementation:**
   290→- Add a `on_session_end` hook in the chat service
   291→- Reuse the `run_silent_memory_turn` from `silent_turn.rs` with a different system prompt focused on session summarization
   292→- Gate behind `[memory] enable_session_summary = true` (default true)
   293→
   294→**System prompt for session-end:**
   295→```
   296→You are a session summarizer. Review the conversation and write a concise summary to memory.
   297→
   298→Focus on:
   299→- What was accomplished (key outcomes and decisions)
   300→- What was left unfinished (follow-up items)
   301→- Any preferences or patterns the user demonstrated
   302→- Technical context that would help resume this work
   303→
   304→Write to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (append, don't overwrite).
   305→Be concise — 5-15 bullet points maximum.
   306→```
   307→
   308→**Tests:**
   309→- Integration test: session end triggers summary write
   310→- Test: summary disabled when config is false
   311→- Test: empty session (no messages) doesn't trigger summary
   312→

   315→## Part 3: Deployment Story ("Runs Anywhere for $5")
   316→
   317→This is more narrative than engineering, but a few concrete deliverables make the story credible.

    14→/// deliberately does **not** include the absolute `SKILL.md` path: the model
    15→/// should activate a skill by calling the native `read_skill` tool with the
    16→/// skill name, which resolves through the same discoverer the prompt block
    17→/// was built from.
    18→pub fn generate_skills_prompt(skills: &[SkillMetadata]) -> String {
    19→    if skills.is_empty() {
    20→        return String::new();
    21→    }
    22→
    23→    let mut out = String::from("## Available Skills\n\n<available_skills>\n");
    24→    for skill in skills {
    25→        let source = if skill.source.as_ref() == Some(&SkillSource::Plugin) {
    26→            "plugin"
    27→        } else {
    28→            "skill"
    29→        };
    30→        out.push_str(&format!(
    31→            "<skill name=\"{}\" source=\"{}\">\n{}\n</skill>\n",
    32→            skill.name, source, skill.description,
    33→        ));
    34→    }
    35→    out.push_str("</available_skills>\n\n");
    36→    // Format the per-subdir list directly from the shared SIDECAR_SUBDIRS
    37→    // constant so adding a subdir in `moltis_skills::SIDECAR_SUBDIRS`
    38→    // automatically updates the instruction. No drift between what the
    39→    // prompt advertises and what the read tool actually walks.
    40→    let subdir_list = SIDECAR_SUBDIRS
    41→        .iter()
    42→        .map(|s| format!("{s}/"))
    43→        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
    44→        .join(", ");
    45→    out.push_str(&format!(
    46→        "To activate a skill, call the `{READ_SKILL_TOOL_NAME}` tool with its name \
    47→         (e.g. `{READ_SKILL_TOOL_NAME}(name=\"<skill-name>\")`). To load a sidecar \
    48→         file inside a skill directory ({subdir_list}), pass the `file_path` \
    49→         argument as well \
    50→         (e.g. `{READ_SKILL_TOOL_NAME}(name=\"<skill-name>\", file_path=\"references/api.md\")`).\n\n",
    51→    ));
    52→    out
    53→}

    70→        // shared constant means adding a new subdir in one place is enough

    63→        "Create a new personal skill. Writes a SKILL.md file to <data_dir>/skills/<name>/. \
    64→         This is persistent workspace storage (not sandbox ~/skills). \
    65→         The skill will be available on the next message automatically."
    66→    }
    67→
    68→    fn parameters_schema(&self) -> Value {
    69→        json!({
    70→            "type": "object",
    71→            "required": ["name", "description", "body"],
    72→            "properties": {
    73→                "name": {
    74→                    "type": "string",
    75→                    "description": "Skill name (lowercase, hyphens, 1-64 chars)"
    76→                },
    77→                "description": {
    78→                    "type": "string",
    79→                    "description": "Short human-readable description"
    80→                },
    81→                "body": {
    82→                    "type": "string",
    83→                    "description": "Markdown instructions for the skill"
    84→                },
    85→                "allowed_tools": {

    95→        let name = params
    96→            .get("name")
    97→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
    98→            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("missing 'name'"))?;
    99→        let description = params
   100→            .get("description")
   101→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   102→            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("missing 'description'"))?;
   103→        let body = params
   104→            .get("body")
   105→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())

   107→        let allowed_tools: Vec<String> = params
   108→            .get("allowed_tools")
   109→            .and_then(|v| v.as_array())

   111→                arr.iter()
   112→                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))
   113→                    .collect()

   115→            .unwrap_or_default();
   116→
   117→        if !moltis_skills::parse::validate_name(name) {

   120→            ))

   122→        }
   123→
   124→        let skill_dir = self.skills_dir().join(name);
   125→        if skill_dir.exists() {
   126→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
   127→                "skill '{name}' already exists; use update_skill to modify it"
   128→            ))
   129→            .into());

   132→        let checkpoint = self
   133→            .checkpoints

   139→        Ok(json!({

   145→}

   256→/// Tool that deletes a personal skill from `<data_dir>/skills/`.
   257→pub struct DeleteSkillTool {
   258→    data_dir: PathBuf,
   259→    checkpoints: CheckpointManager,
   260→}
   261→
   262→impl DeleteSkillTool {
   263→    pub fn new(data_dir: PathBuf) -> Self {
   264→        let checkpoints = CheckpointManager::new(data_dir.clone());
   265→        Self {
   266→            data_dir,
   267→            checkpoints,
   268→        }
   269→    }
   270→
   271→    fn skills_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
   272→        self.data_dir.join("skills")
   273→    }
   274→}
   275→
   276→#[async_trait]
   277→impl AgentTool for DeleteSkillTool {
   278→    fn name(&self) -> &str {
   279→        "delete_skill"
   280→    }
   281→
   282→    fn description(&self) -> &str {
   283→        "Delete a personal skill. Removes the full skill directory, including supplementary files."
   284→    }
   285→
   286→    fn parameters_schema(&self) -> Value {
   287→        json!({
   288→            "type": "object",
   289→            "required": ["name"],
   290→            "properties": {
   291→                "name": {
   292→                    "type": "string",
   293→                    "description": "Skill name to delete"
   294→                }
   295→            }
   296→        })
   297→    }
   298→
   299→    async fn execute(&self, params: Value) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
   300→        let name = params
   301→            .get("name")
   302→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   303→            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("missing 'name'"))?;
   304→
   305→        if !moltis_skills::parse::validate_name(name) {
   306→            return Err(Error::message(format!("invalid skill name '{name}'")).into());
   307→        }
   308→
   309→        let skill_dir = self.skills_dir().join(name);
   310→
   311→        // Only allow deleting from the personal skills directory.
   312→        let canonical_base = self
   313→            .skills_dir()
   314→            .canonicalize()
   315→            .unwrap_or_else(|_| self.skills_dir().clone());
   316→        let canonical_target = skill_dir
   317→            .canonicalize()
   318→            .unwrap_or_else(|_| skill_dir.clone());
   319→        if !canonical_target.starts_with(&canonical_base) {
   320→            return Err(Error::message("can only delete personal skills").into());
   321→        }
   322→
   323→        if !skill_dir.exists() {
   324→            return Err(Error::message(format!("skill '{name}' not found")).into());
   325→        }
   326→
   327→        let checkpoint = self
   328→            .checkpoints
   329→            .checkpoint_path(&skill_dir, "delete_skill")
   330→            .await?;
   331→        tokio::fs::remove_dir_all(&skill_dir).await?;
   332→
   333→        Ok(json!({
   334→            "deleted": true,
   335→            "checkpointId": checkpoint.id,
   336→        }))
   337→    }
   338→}

   383→         under references/, templates/, assets/, and scripts/. To read those, \
   384→         call again with the file_path argument \
   385→         (e.g. file_path=\"references/api.md\"). Nested file_paths such as \
   386→         \"references/subdir/deep.md\" are supported even if the listing only \
   387→         shows the first level. Binary files return a structured response \
   388→         with { is_binary: true, bytes }. Use the skill names listed in the \
   389→         <available_skills> system-prompt block."
   390→    }
   391→
   392→    fn parameters_schema(&self) -> Value {
   393→        json!({
   394→            "type": "object",
   395→            "required": ["name"],
   396→            "properties": {
   397→                "name": {
   398→                    "type": "string",
   399→                    "description": "Skill name (use the names from <available_skills>)"
   400→                },
   401→                "file_path": {
   402→                    "type": "string",
   403→                    "description": "Optional: relative path to a sidecar file inside the skill directory (e.g. 'references/api.md'). Omit to read the main SKILL.md body."
   404→                }
   405→            }
   406→        })
   407→    }
   408→
   409→    async fn execute(&self, params: Value) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
   410→        let name = params
   411→            .get("name")
   412→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   413→            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("missing 'name'"))?;
   414→        let file_path = params.get("file_path").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
   415→
   416→        let skills = self.discoverer.discover().await?;
   417→        let meta = skills.iter().find(|s| s.name == name).ok_or_else(|| {
   418→            let available: Vec<&str> = skills.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();
   419→            let hint = if available.is_empty() {
   420→                "no skills are currently available".to_string()
   421→            } else {
   422→                format!("available skills: {}", available.join(", "))
   423→            };
   424→            Error::message(format!(
   425→                "skill '{name}' not found ({hint}). Use one of the names listed \
   426→                 in <available_skills>."
   427→            ))
   428→        })?;
   429→
   430→        if let Some(rel) = file_path {
   431→            // Plugin-backed skills can be a single `.md` file rather than
   432→            // a directory containing SKILL.md. Reject sidecar requests on
   433→            // such skills with a clear error — otherwise `read_sidecar`
   434→            // would canonicalise the `.md` file and join the relative
   435→            // path, producing nonsense like `/plugin/demo.md/references/api.md`
   436→            // that would fail with an opaque I/O error.
   437→            if meta.source.as_ref() == Some(&SkillSource::Plugin)
   438→                && tokio::fs::metadata(&meta.path)
   439→                    .await
   440→                    .map(|m| m.is_file())
   441→                    .unwrap_or(false)
   442→            {
   443→                return Err(Error::message(format!(
   444→                    "plugin skill '{name}' is a single .md file and has no \
   445→                     sidecar directory; omit file_path to read the body"
   446→                ))
   447→                .into());
   448→            }
   449→            return read_sidecar(name, &meta.path, rel).await;
   450→        }
   451→
   452→        read_primary(name, meta).await
   453→    }
   454→}
   455→
   456→/// Read the main SKILL.md body (or the plugin's `.md` file) plus the list of
   457→/// sidecar files available in `references/`, `templates/`, `assets/`, and
   458→/// `scripts/`. The response also surfaces frontmatter metadata fields
   459→/// (`license`, `homepage`, `compatibility`, `allowed_tools`, `display_name`)
   460→/// so the agent can make informed activation decisions without a second call.
   461→async fn read_primary(
   462→    name: &str,
   463→    meta: &moltis_skills::types::SkillMetadata,
   464→) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
   465→    let is_plugin = meta.source.as_ref() == Some(&SkillSource::Plugin);
   466→
   467→    // Reject a symlinked skill root the same way `read_sidecar` and
   468→    // `write_sidecar_files` do. Without this guard, a symlink like
   469→    // `~/.moltis/skills/malicious -> /etc` would canonicalise silently
   470→    // and the rest of the read path would serve whatever the target
   471→    // resolves to. Defence in depth: the discoverer should not hand us a
   472→    // symlinked root, but the tool enforces the invariant regardless.
   473→    match tokio::fs::symlink_metadata(&meta.path).await {
   474→        Ok(m) if m.file_type().is_symlink() => {
   475→            return Err(
   476→                Error::message(format!("skill '{name}' directory must not be a symlink")).into(),
   477→            );
   478→        },
   479→        Ok(_) => {},
   480→        Err(e) => {
   481→            return Err(Error::message(format!("skill '{name}' path not accessible: {e}")).into());
   482→        },
   483→    }
   484→
   485→    // Detect whether a plugin-backed skill is a single `.md` file (rather
   486→    // than a SKILL.md-in-a-directory) via async metadata so the read path
   487→    // stays fully non-blocking — no synchronous `Path::is_file` inside an
   488→    // async function.
   489→    let plugin_as_file = is_plugin
   490→        && tokio::fs::metadata(&meta.path)
   491→            .await
   492→            .map(|m| m.is_file())
   493→            .unwrap_or(false);
   494→
   495→    // Plugin skills can be backed by a single `.md` file rather than a
   496→    // directory containing SKILL.md (see `prompt_gen.rs`). Handle both shapes.
   497→    let (loaded_meta, body, linked_files, effective_dir) = if plugin_as_file {
   498→        // Size check *before* reading the whole file so we never buffer a
   499→        // multi-megabyte `.md` into memory only to reject it. Mirrors the
   500→        // defence-in-depth posture `read_sidecar` uses for sidecar files.
   501→        let file_meta = tokio::fs::metadata(&meta.path).await.map_err(|e| {
   502→            Error::message(format!(
   503→                "failed to stat plugin skill '{name}' at {}: {e}",
   504→                meta.path.display()
   505→            ))
   506→        })?;
   507→        if file_meta.len() > MAX_SKILL_BODY_BYTES as u64 {
   508→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
   509→                "plugin skill '{name}' body exceeds maximum size of \
   510→                 {MAX_SKILL_BODY_BYTES} bytes ({} bytes on disk)",
   511→                file_meta.len()
   512→            ))
   513→            .into());
   514→        }
   515→        let raw = tokio::fs::read_to_string(&meta.path).await.map_err(|e| {
   516→            Error::message(format!(
   517→                "failed to read plugin skill '{name}' at {}: {e}",
   518→                meta.path.display()
   519→            ))
   520→        })?;
   521→        // Strip any optional YAML frontmatter so the model sees clean
   522→        // markdown — without this, plugin-backed skills that follow the
   523→        // SKILL.md format return `---\nname: ...\n---` noise in the body.
   524→        // Mirrors what `load_skill_from_path` does for directory-backed
   525→        // skills via `parse::parse_skill`.
   526→        let body = moltis_skills::parse::strip_optional_frontmatter(&raw).to_string();
   527→        let effective_dir = meta
   528→            .path
   529→            .parent()
   530→            .map(Path::to_path_buf)
   531→            .unwrap_or_else(|| meta.path.clone());
   532→        // Plugin .md files don't carry full frontmatter in the discovered
   533→        // metadata — fall back to the discoverer's stub metadata.
   534→        (meta.clone(), body, Vec::new(), effective_dir)
   535→    } else {
   536→        let canonical_skill_dir = tokio::fs::canonicalize(&meta.path).await.map_err(|e| {
   537→            Error::message(format!("skill directory not accessible for '{name}': {e}"))
   538→        })?;
   539→
   540→        // Apply the same defensive ceiling to directory-backed SKILL.md
   541→        // files so the plugin and directory paths have symmetric limits.
   542→        let skill_md_path = canonical_skill_dir.join("SKILL.md");
   543→        if let Ok(m) = tokio::fs::metadata(&skill_md_path).await
   544→            && m.len() > MAX_SKILL_BODY_BYTES as u64
   545→        {
   546→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
   547→                "skill '{name}' SKILL.md exceeds maximum size of \
   548→                 {MAX_SKILL_BODY_BYTES} bytes ({} bytes on disk)",
   549→                m.len()
   550→            ))
   551→            .into());
   552→        }
   553→
   554→        let content = moltis_skills::registry::load_skill_from_path(&canonical_skill_dir)
   555→            .await
   556→            .map_err(|e| Error::message(format!("failed to load skill '{name}': {e}")))?;
   557→        let linked = list_skill_sidecar_files(&canonical_skill_dir).await?;
   558→        (content.metadata, content.body, linked, canonical_skill_dir)
   559→    };
   560→
   561→    // Warn on injection patterns (do not block).
   562→    let hits = moltis_skills::safety::scan_skill_body(name, &body);
   563→    if !hits.is_empty() {
   564→        tracing::warn!(
   565→            skill = %name,
   566→            patterns = ?hits,
   567→            "skill body contains potential prompt-injection patterns"
   568→        );
   569→    }
   570→
   571→    let source_label = match meta.source.as_ref() {
   572→        Some(SkillSource::Project) => "project",
   573→        Some(SkillSource::Personal) => "personal",
   574→        Some(SkillSource::Plugin) => "plugin",
   575→        Some(SkillSource::Registry) => "registry",
   576→        None => "unknown",
   577→    };
   578→
   579→    // Build the response as a Map directly to avoid the
   580→    // `as_object_mut().expect()` pattern that workspace clippy lints on.
   581→    // Optional metadata fields are only included when set so the agent
   582→    // doesn't wade through empty keys.
   583→    let mut response = serde_json::Map::new();
   584→    response.insert("name".into(), json!(name));
   585→    response.insert("description".into(), json!(loaded_meta.description));
   586→    response.insert("source".into(), json!(source_label));
   587→    response.insert("body".into(), json!(body));
   588→    response.insert("bytes".into(), json!(body.len()));
   589→    response.insert(
   590→        "skill_dir_name".into(),
   591→        json!(
   592→            effective_dir
   593→                .file_name()
   594→                .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
   595→                .unwrap_or("")
   596→        ),
   597→    );
   598→
   599→    if let Some(display_name) = &loaded_meta.display_name {
   600→        response.insert("display_name".into(), json!(display_name));
   601→    }
   602→    if let Some(license) = &loaded_meta.license {
   603→        response.insert("license".into(), json!(license));
   604→    }
   605→    if let Some(homepage) = &loaded_meta.homepage {
   606→        response.insert("homepage".into(), json!(homepage));
   607→    }
   608→    if let Some(compatibility) = &loaded_meta.compatibility {
   609→        response.insert("compatibility".into(), json!(compatibility));
   610→    }
   611→    if !loaded_meta.allowed_tools.is_empty() {
   612→        response.insert("allowed_tools".into(), json!(loaded_meta.allowed_tools));
   613→    }
   614→    if !linked_files.is_empty() {
   615→        response.insert(
   616→            "usage_hint".into(),
   617→            json!(
   618→                "To view a linked file, call read_skill again with file_path \
   619→                 set to one of the paths in linked_files (e.g. \
   620→                 file_path=\"references/api.md\"). Nested paths inside those \
   621→                 directories are also supported."
   622→            ),
   623→        );
   624→    }
   625→    // `linked_files` goes last so tools that pretty-print the response
   626→    // surface metadata first.
   627→    response.insert("linked_files".into(), json!(linked_files));
   628→
   629→    Ok(Value::Object(response))
   630→}
   631→
   632→/// Read a single sidecar file inside a skill directory.
   633→///
   634→/// Supports arbitrary-depth `Component::Normal`-only relative paths (e.g.
   635→/// `references/subdir/deep.md`). Binary files return a structured
   636→/// `{ is_binary: true, bytes }` response instead of failing on UTF-8 decode.
   637→/// If the file doesn't exist, returns a helpful listing of the sidecar files
   638→/// that do exist under this skill.
   639→async fn read_sidecar(name: &str, skill_dir: &Path, rel: &str) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
   640→    let relative = normalize_relative_skill_file_path(rel)?;
   641→
   642→    // Reject a symlinked skill directory to stay consistent with
   643→    // `write_sidecar_files`. Without this, a symlinked skill root
   644→    // (e.g. `~/.moltis/skills/malicious -> /etc`) would pass the later
   645→    // canonical-prefix check because `canonicalize` resolves the symlink
   646→    // and the subsequent `starts_with` comparison succeeds against the
   647→    // resolved target.
   648→    match tokio::fs::symlink_metadata(skill_dir).await {
   649→        Ok(meta) if meta.file_type().is_symlink() => {
   650→            return Err(
   651→                Error::message(format!("skill '{name}' directory must not be a symlink")).into(),
   652→            );
   653→        },
   654→        Ok(_) => {},
   655→        Err(e) => {
   656→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
   657→                "skill directory not accessible for '{name}': {e}"
   658→            ))
   659→            .into());
   660→        },
   661→    }
   662→
   663→    let canonical_skill_dir = tokio::fs::canonicalize(skill_dir)
   664→        .await
   665→        .map_err(|e| Error::message(format!("skill directory not accessible for '{name}': {e}")))?;
   666→
   667→    let target = canonical_skill_dir.join(&relative);
   668→
   669→    // Check existence before canonicalising so we can return a helpful
   670→    // listing instead of an opaque I/O error when the file is missing.
   671→    match tokio::fs::symlink_metadata(&target).await {
   672→        Ok(_) => {},
   673→        Err(err) if err.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
   674→            let available = list_skill_sidecar_files(&canonical_skill_dir).await?;
   675→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
   676→                "sidecar file '{}' not found in skill '{name}'. \
   677→                 Available sidecar files: {}",
   678→                relative.display(),
   679→                if available.is_empty() {
   680→                    "(none)".to_string()
   681→                } else {
   682→                    available
   683→                        .iter()
   684→                        .filter_map(|v| v.get("path").and_then(|p| p.as_str()))
   685→                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
   686→                        .join(", ")
   687→                }
   688→            ))
   689→            .into());
   690→        },
   691→        Err(e) => {
   692→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
   693→                "sidecar file '{}' not accessible: {e}",
   694→                relative.display()
   695→            ))
   696→            .into());
   697→        },
   698→    }
   699→
   700→    let canonical_target = tokio::fs::canonicalize(&target).await.map_err(|e| {
   701→        Error::message(format!(
   702→            "sidecar file '{}' not accessible: {e}",
   703→            relative.display()
   704→        ))
   705→    })?;
   706→
   707→    if !canonical_target.starts_with(&canonical_skill_dir) {
   708→        return Err(Error::message(format!(
   709→            "sidecar file '{}' is outside the skill directory",
   710→            relative.display()
   711→        ))
   712→        .into());
   713→    }
   714→
   715→    let metadata = tokio::fs::metadata(&canonical_target).await?;
   716→    if !metadata.is_file() {
   717→        return Err(Error::message(format!(
   718→            "sidecar path '{}' is not a regular file",
   719→            relative.display()
   720→        ))
   721→        .into());
   722→    }
   723→    if metadata.len() > MAX_SIDECAR_FILE_BYTES as u64 {
   724→        return Err(Error::message(format!(
   725→            "sidecar file '{}' exceeds maximum size of {MAX_SIDECAR_FILE_BYTES} bytes",
   726→            relative.display()
   727→        ))
   728→        .into());
   729→    }
   730→
   731→    // Try UTF-8; fall back to a structured "binary" response on decode
   732→    // failure (mirrors hermes-agent's `skill_view` behavior).
   733→    let raw = tokio::fs::read(&canonical_target).await.map_err(|e| {
   734→        Error::message(format!(
   735→            "failed to read sidecar file '{}': {e}",
   736→            relative.display()
   737→        ))
   738→    })?;
   739→
   740→    match std::str::from_utf8(&raw) {
   741→        Ok(text) => Ok(json!({
   742→            "name": name,
   743→            "file_path": relative.display().to_string(),
   744→            "bytes": metadata.len(),
   745→            "content": text,
   746→            "is_binary": false,
   747→        })),
   748→        Err(_) => {
   749→            let file_type = canonical_target
   750→                .extension()
   751→                .and_then(|e| e.to_str())
   752→                .map(|s| format!(".{s}"))
   753→                .unwrap_or_default();
   754→            Ok(json!({
   755→                "name": name,
   756→                "file_path": relative.display().to_string(),
   757→                "bytes": metadata.len(),
   758→                "is_binary": true,
   759→                "file_type": file_type,
   760→                "note": format!(
   761→                    "Binary file ({} bytes). Contents omitted — the model \
   762→                     cannot consume binary data directly.",
   763→                    metadata.len()
   764→                ),
   765→            }))
   766→        },
   767→    }
   768→}
   769→
   770→/// Sidecar subdirectories that are walked for the primary-read linked-files
   771→/// listing. Re-exported from [`moltis_skills::SIDECAR_SUBDIRS`] so the prompt
   772→/// generator and the read-side walker stay in lockstep — adding a new entry
   773→/// in the skills crate automatically propagates to both the activation
   774→/// instruction and this walker, eliminating a whole class of drift bugs.
   775→const SIDECAR_SUBDIRS: &[&str] = moltis_skills::SIDECAR_SUBDIRS;
   776→
   777→/// Entry returned by [`list_skill_sidecar_files`]. Sorted-for-determinism and
   778→/// kept as a typed struct so both the primary read path and the sidecar
   779→/// "file not found" error path can reuse it.
   780→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   781→struct SidecarEntry {
   782→    /// Path relative to the skill directory, e.g. `references/api.md`.
   783→    relative_path: String,
   784→    bytes: u64,
   785→}
   786→
   787→impl From<&SidecarEntry> for Value {
   788→    fn from(entry: &SidecarEntry) -> Self {
   789→        json!({
   790→            "path": entry.relative_path,
   791→            "bytes": entry.bytes,
   792→        })
   793→    }
   794→}
   795→
   796→/// One-level-deep walk of `<skill_dir>/{references,templates,assets,scripts}`.
   797→///
   798→/// Returns a sorted (by relative path) list of entries, capped at
   799→/// [`MAX_SIDECAR_FILES_PER_CALL`]. Directory entries, symlinks, hidden files
   800→/// (dotfiles), and unreadable entries are skipped silently so the listing
   801→/// only shows real in-skill files the agent can actually consume.
   802→async fn list_skill_sidecar_files(skill_dir: &Path) -> crate::Result<Vec<Value>> {
   803→    let mut entries = collect_sidecar_entries(skill_dir).await?;
   804→    // Sort for deterministic output — makes tests stable and the agent's
   805→    // reasoning traces reproducible across runs.
   806→    entries.sort_by(|a, b| a.relative_path.cmp(&b.relative_path));
   807→    Ok(entries.iter().map(Value::from).collect())
   808→}
   809→
   810→async fn collect_sidecar_entries(skill_dir: &Path) -> crate::Result<Vec<SidecarEntry>> {
   811→    let mut out: Vec<SidecarEntry> = Vec::new();
   812→
   813→    for sub in SIDECAR_SUBDIRS {
   814→        // Stop early if the global cap is already exhausted so we don't
   815→        // over-report, but *do* enter each subdir as long as it has free
   816→        // budget — the per-subdir cap below guarantees every populated
   817→        // subdirectory gets its fair share even when one dir contains
   818→        // hundreds of files.
   819→        if out.len() >= MAX_SIDECAR_FILES_PER_CALL {
   820→            break;
   821→        }
   822→        let dir = skill_dir.join(sub);
   823→        // Use `tokio::fs::read_dir` directly and treat a missing or
   824→        // unreadable subdirectory as "no entries" — avoids a synchronous
   825→        // `Path::is_dir()` stat inside this async function.
   826→        let mut entries = match tokio::fs::read_dir(&dir).await {
   827→            Ok(e) => e,
   828→            Err(_) => continue,
   829→        };
   830→        let mut this_subdir = 0usize;
   831→        while let Some(entry) = entries.next_entry().await? {
   832→            // Enforce both the per-subdir cap (so `references/` can't
   833→            // swallow the entire listing and hide `templates/` or
   834→            // `scripts/`) and the global cap (so a pathological skill
   835→            // can't return thousands of entries).
   836→            if this_subdir >= MAX_SIDECAR_FILES_PER_SUBDIR
   837→                || out.len() >= MAX_SIDECAR_FILES_PER_CALL
   838→            {
   839→                break;
   840→            }
   841→            // Reject symlinks so the listing only shows real in-skill files.
   842→            let file_type = match entry.file_type().await {
   843→                Ok(ft) => ft,
   844→                Err(_) => continue,
   845→            };
   846→            if !file_type.is_file() {
   847→                continue;
   848→            }
   849→            let meta = match entry.metadata().await {
   850→                Ok(m) => m,
   851→                Err(_) => continue,
   852→            };
   853→            let file_name = match entry.file_name().into_string() {
   854→                Ok(name) => name,
   855→                Err(_) => continue,
   856→            };
   857→            if file_name.starts_with('.') {
   858→                continue;
   859→            }
   860→            out.push(SidecarEntry {
   861→                relative_path: format!("{sub}/{file_name}"),
   862→                bytes: meta.len(),
   863→            });
   864→            this_subdir += 1;
   865→        }
   866→    }
   867→
   868→    Ok(out)
   869→}
   870→
   871→/// Tool that writes supplementary text files inside an existing personal skill.
   872→pub struct WriteSkillFilesTool {
   873→    data_dir: PathBuf,
   874→    checkpoints: CheckpointManager,
   875→}
   876→
   877→impl WriteSkillFilesTool {
   878→    pub fn new(data_dir: PathBuf) -> Self {
   879→        let checkpoints = CheckpointManager::new(data_dir.clone());
   880→        Self {
   881→            data_dir,
   882→            checkpoints,
   883→        }
   884→    }
   885→
   886→    fn skills_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
   887→        self.data_dir.join("skills")
   888→    }
   889→}
   890→
   891→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   892→struct ValidatedSkillFile {
   893→    relative_path: PathBuf,
   894→    content: String,
   895→}
   896→
   897→#[async_trait]
   898→impl AgentTool for WriteSkillFilesTool {
   899→    fn name(&self) -> &str {
   900→        "write_skill_files"
   901→    }
   902→
   903→    fn description(&self) -> &str {
   904→        "Write supplementary UTF-8 text files inside an existing personal skill directory. \
   905→         This tool is disabled by default and only appears when skills.enable_agent_sidecar_files is enabled."
   906→    }
   907→
   908→    fn parameters_schema(&self) -> Value {
   909→        json!({
   910→            "type": "object",
   911→            "required": ["name", "files"],
   912→            "properties": {
   913→                "name": {
   914→                    "type": "string",
   915→                    "description": "Existing skill name to update"
   916→                },
   917→                "files": {
   918→                    "type": "array",
   919→                    "description": "Supplementary text files to write inside the skill directory",
   920→                    "minItems": 1,
   921→                    "maxItems": MAX_SIDECAR_FILES_PER_CALL,
   922→                    "items": {
   923→                        "type": "object",
   924→                        "required": ["path", "content"],
   925→                        "properties": {
   926→                            "path": {
   927→                                "type": "string",
   928→                                "description": "Relative path inside the skill directory"
   929→                            },
   930→                            "content": {
   931→                                "type": "string",
   932→                                "description": "UTF-8 text content to write"
   933→                            }
   934→                        }
   935→                    }
   936→                }
   937→            }
   938→        })
   939→    }

   941→    async fn execute(&self, params: Value) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
   942→        let name = params
   943→            .get("name")
   944→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
   945→            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("missing 'name'"))?;
   946→
   947→        if !moltis_skills::parse::validate_name(name) {
   948→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
   949→                "invalid skill name '{name}': must be 1-64 lowercase alphanumeric/hyphen chars"
   950→            ))
   951→            .into());
   952→        }
   953→
   954→        let files = params
   955→            .get("files")
   956→            .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
   957→            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("missing 'files'"))?;
   958→        let validated = validate_sidecar_files(files)?;
   959→
   960→        let skill_dir = self.skills_dir().join(name);
   961→        if !skill_dir.exists() {
   962→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
   963→                "skill '{name}' does not exist; use create_skill first"
   964→            ))
   965→            .into());
   966→        }
   967→
   968→        let checkpoint = self
   969→            .checkpoints
   970→            .checkpoint_path(&skill_dir, "write_skill_files")
   971→            .await?;
   972→        write_sidecar_files(&skill_dir, &validated).await?;
   973→        audit_sidecar_file_write(&self.data_dir, name, &validated);
   974→
   975→        Ok(json!({
   976→            "written": true,
   977→            "path": skill_dir.display().to_string(),
   978→            "checkpointId": checkpoint.id,
   979→            "files_written": validated.len(),
   980→            "files": validated.iter().map(|file| file.relative_path.display().to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
   981→        }))
   982→    }
   983→}
   984→
   985→fn build_skill_md(name: &str, description: &str, body: &str, allowed_tools: &[String]) -> String {
   986→    let mut frontmatter = format!("---\nname: {name}\ndescription: {description}\n");
   987→    if !allowed_tools.is_empty() {
   988→        frontmatter.push_str("allowed_tools:\n");
   989→        for tool in allowed_tools {
   990→            frontmatter.push_str(&format!("  - {tool}\n"));
   991→        }
   992→    }
   993→    frontmatter.push_str("---\n\n");
   994→    frontmatter.push_str(body);
   995→    if !body.ends_with('\n') {
   996→        frontmatter.push('\n');
   997→    }
   998→    frontmatter
   999→}
  1000→
  1001→async fn write_skill(skill_dir: &Path, content: &str) -> crate::Result<()> {
  1002→    tokio::fs::create_dir_all(skill_dir).await?;
  1003→    tokio::fs::write(skill_dir.join("SKILL.md"), content).await?;
  1004→    Ok(())
  1005→}
  1006→
  1007→fn validate_sidecar_files(files: &[Value]) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<ValidatedSkillFile>> {
  1008→    if files.is_empty() {
  1009→        return Err(Error::message("at least one file is required").into());
  1010→    }
  1011→    if files.len() > MAX_SIDECAR_FILES_PER_CALL {
  1012→        return Err(Error::message(format!(
  1013→            "too many files: maximum is {MAX_SIDECAR_FILES_PER_CALL}"
  1014→        ))
  1015→        .into());
  1016→    }
  1017→
  1018→    let mut total_bytes = 0usize;
  1019→    let mut seen_paths = HashSet::new();
  1020→    let mut validated = Vec::with_capacity(files.len());
  1021→
  1022→    for file in files {
  1023→        let path = file
  1024→            .get("path")
  1025→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
  1026→            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("each file needs a string 'path'"))?;
  1027→        let content = file
  1028→            .get("content")
  1029→            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
  1030→            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("each file needs a string 'content'"))?;
  1031→
  1032→        let relative_path = normalize_relative_skill_file_path(path)?;
  1033→        if !seen_paths.insert(relative_path.clone()) {
  1034→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
  1035→                "duplicate file path '{}'",
  1036→                relative_path.display()
  1037→            ))
  1038→            .into());
  1039→        }
  1040→
  1041→        let file_bytes = content.len();
  1042→        if file_bytes > MAX_SIDECAR_FILE_BYTES {
  1043→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
  1044→                "file '{}' exceeds maximum size of {MAX_SIDECAR_FILE_BYTES} bytes",
  1045→                relative_path.display()
  1046→            ))
  1047→            .into());
  1048→        }
  1049→
  1050→        total_bytes += file_bytes;
  1051→        if total_bytes > MAX_SIDECAR_TOTAL_BYTES {
  1052→            return Err(Error::message(format!(
  1053→                "total file content exceeds maximum size of {MAX_SIDECAR_TOTAL_BYTES} bytes"
  1054→            ))
  1055→            .into());
  1056→        }
  1057→
  1058→        validated.push(ValidatedSkillFile {
  1059→            relative_path,
  1060→            content: content.to_string(),
  1061→        });
  1062→    }
  1063→
  1064→    Ok(validated)
  1065→}
  1066→
  1067→fn normalize_relative_skill_file_path(path: &str) -> anyhow::Result<PathBuf> {
  1068→    let trimmed = path.trim();
  1069→    if trimmed.is_empty() {
  1070→        return Err(Error::message("file path must not be empty").into());
  1071→    }
  1072→
  1073→    let candidate = Path::new(trimmed);
  1074→    if candidate.is_absolute() {
  1075→        return Err(Error::message("file path must be relative").into());
  1076→    }
  1077→
  1078→    let mut normalized = PathBuf::new();
  1079→    for component in candidate.components() {
  1080→        match component {
  1081→            Component::Normal(segment) => {
  1082→                let Some(segment_str) = segment.to_str() else {
  1083→                    return Err(Error::message("file path must be valid UTF-8").into());
  1084→                };
  1085→                if segment_str.starts_with('.') {
  1086→                    return Err(Error::message(format!(
  1087→                        "hidden path components are not allowed: '{trimmed}'"
  1088→                    ))
  1089→                    .into());
  1090→                }
  1091→                normalized.push(segment);
  1092→            },
  1093→            Component::CurDir => {},
  1094→            Component::ParentDir | Component::RootDir | Component::Prefix(_) => {
  1095→                return Err(Error::message("path traversal is not allowed").into());
  1096→            },
  1097→        }
  1098→    }
  1099→
  1100→    let Some(file_name) = normalized.file_name().and_then(|name| name.to_str()) else {
  1101→        return Err(Error::message("file path must name a file").into());
  1102→    };
  1103→
  1104→    if file_name.eq_ignore_ascii_case("SKILL.md") {
  1105→        return Err(
  1106→            Error::message("SKILL.md must be managed with create_skill/update_skill").into(),
  1107→        );
  1108→    }
  1109→
  1110→    Ok(normalized)
  1111→}
  1112→
  1113→async fn write_sidecar_files(skill_dir: &Path, files: &[ValidatedSkillFile]) -> crate::Result<()> {
  1114→    // Anchor the confinement check to the canonical *skills root*, not the
  1115→    // skill directory itself.  If `<data_dir>/skills/<name>` were a symlink
  1116→    // pointing outside the tree, using `canonicalize(skill_dir)` as the base
  1117→    // would silently accept writes to the symlink target.
  1118→    let skills_root = skill_dir
  1119→        .parent()
  1120→        .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("invalid skill directory"))?;
  1121→    let canonical_skills_root = tokio::fs::canonicalize(skills_root).await?;
  1122→
  1123→    // Reject a skill directory that is itself a symlink.
  1124→    let skill_meta = tokio::fs::symlink_metadata(skill_dir).await?;
  1125→    if skill_meta.file_type().is_symlink() {
  1126→        return Err(Error::message("skill directory must not be a symlink"));
  1127→    }
  1128→
  1129→    let canonical_base = tokio::fs::canonicalize(skill_dir).await?;
  1130→    if !canonical_base.starts_with(&canonical_skills_root) {
  1131→        return Err(Error::message("skill directory is outside the skills root"));
  1132→    }
  1133→
  1134→    let mut written_paths: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
  1135→
  1136→    for file in files {
  1137→        let target = skill_dir.join(&file.relative_path);
  1138→        let parent = target
  1139→            .parent()
  1140→            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message("invalid file path"))?;
  1141→
  1142→        // Validate path ancestry *before* creating directories so a symlinked
  1143→        // intermediate cannot cause out-of-tree directory creation.
  1144→        validate_no_symlinks_in_ancestry(skill_dir, &file.relative_path).await?;
  1145→
  1146→        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(parent).await?;
  1147→
  1148→        let canonical_parent = tokio::fs::canonicalize(parent).await?;
  1149→        if !canonical_parent.starts_with(&canonical_base) {
  1150→            rollback_written_files(&written_paths).await;
  1151→            return Err(Error::message(
  1152→                "can only write inside the personal skill directory",
  1153→            ));
  1154→        }
  1155→
  1156→        if let Ok(metadata) = tokio::fs::symlink_metadata(&target).await {
  1157→            if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() {
  1158→                rollback_written_files(&written_paths).await;
  1159→                return Err(Error::message(format!(
  1160→                    "refusing to write through symlink '{}'",
  1161→                    file.relative_path.display()
  1162→                )));
  1163→            }
  1164→            if metadata.is_dir() {
  1165→                rollback_written_files(&written_paths).await;
  1166→                return Err(Error::message(format!(
  1167→                    "target '{}' is a directory",
  1168→                    file.relative_path.display()
  1169→                )));
  1170→            }
  1171→        }
  1172→
  1173→        let Some(file_name) = file
  1174→            .relative_path
  1175→            .file_name()
  1176→            .and_then(|value| value.to_str())
  1177→        else {
  1178→            rollback_written_files(&written_paths).await;
  1179→            return Err(Error::message("invalid file name"));
  1180→        };
  1181→        let temp_name = format!(".{file_name}.moltis-tmp-{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4());
  1182→        let temp_path = parent.join(temp_name);
  1183→
  1184→        tokio::fs::write(&temp_path, &file.content).await?;
  1185→        if let Err(error) = tokio::fs::rename(&temp_path, &target).await {
  1186→            let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(&temp_path).await;
  1187→            rollback_written_files(&written_paths).await;
  1188→            return Err(error.into());
  1189→        }
  1190→        written_paths.push(target);
  1191→    }
  1192→
  1193→    Ok(())
  1194→}
  1195→
  1196→/// Walk from `base` through the existing intermediate components of
  1197→/// `relative_path` (excluding the final file component) and reject any
  1198→/// symlink.  This prevents `create_dir_all` from following a symlinked
  1199→/// intermediate and creating directories outside the skill tree.
  1200→async fn validate_no_symlinks_in_ancestry(base: &Path, relative_path: &Path) -> crate::Result<()> {
  1201→    let components: Vec<_> = relative_path.components().collect();
  1202→    // Only check parent components — the last component is the file itself.
  1203→    let parent_components = components.len().saturating_sub(1);
  1204→    let mut current = base.to_path_buf();
  1205→    for component in components.iter().take(parent_components) {
  1206→        if let Component::Normal(segment) = component {
  1207→            current.push(segment);
  1208→            match tokio::fs::symlink_metadata(&current).await {
  1209→                Ok(meta) if meta.file_type().is_symlink() => {
  1210→                    return Err(Error::message(format!(
  1211→                        "refusing to traverse symlink at '{}'",
  1212→                        current.display()
  1213→                    )));
  1214→                },
  1215→                Ok(_) => {},
  1216→                // Path doesn't exist yet — safe to stop; create_dir_all will
  1217→                // create it as a real directory.
  1218→                Err(_) => break,
  1219→            }
  1220→        }
  1221→    }
  1222→    Ok(())
  1223→}
  1224→
  1225→/// Best-effort removal of already-written files when a batch fails mid-way.
  1226→async fn rollback_written_files(paths: &[PathBuf]) {
  1227→    for path in paths.iter().rev() {
  1228→        let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(path).await;
  1229→    }
  1230→}
  1231→
  1232→fn audit_sidecar_file_write(data_dir: &Path, skill_name: &str, files: &[ValidatedSkillFile]) {
  1233→    let dir = data_dir.join("logs");
  1234→    let path = dir.join("security-audit.jsonl");
  1235→    let now_ms = std::time::SystemTime::now()
  1236→        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
  1237→        .unwrap_or_default()
  1238→        .as_millis() as u64;
  1239→    let line = serde_json::json!({
  1240→        "ts": now_ms,
  1241→        "event": "skills.sidecar_files.write",
  1242→        "details": {
  1243→            "skill": skill_name,
  1244→            "files": files.iter().map(|file| {
  1245→                serde_json::json!({
  1246→                    "path": file.relative_path.display().to_string(),
  1247→                    "bytes": file.content.len(),
  1248→                })
  1249→            }).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
  1250→        },
  1251→    })
  1252→    .to_string();
  1253→
  1254→    if let Err(err) = (|| -> std::io::Result<()> {
  1255→        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir)?;
  1256→        let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
  1257→            .create(true)
  1258→            .append(true)
  1259→            .open(path)?;
  1260→        use std::io::Write as _;
  1261→        writeln!(file, "{line}")?;
  1262→        Ok(())
  1263→    })() {
  1264→        tracing::warn!(
  1265→            error = %err,
  1266→            skill = skill_name,
  1267→            "failed to write sidecar-file audit entry"
  1268→        );
  1269→    }
  1270→}

   130→    pub place: Option<String>,

   135→
   136→impl GeoLocation {
   137→    /// Create a new `GeoLocation` stamped with the current time.
   138→    pub fn now(latitude: f64, longitude: f64, place: Option<String>) -> Self {
   139→        let ts = std::time::SystemTime::now()
   140→            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
   141→            .unwrap_or_default()
   142→            .as_secs() as i64;
   143→        Self {
   144→            latitude,
   145→            longitude,
   146→            place,
   147→            updated_at: Some(ts),
   148→        }
   149→    }
   150→}

   152→impl std::fmt::Display for GeoLocation {
   153→    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
   154→        if let Some(ref place) = self.place {
   155→            write!(f, "{place}")?;
   156→        } else {
   157→            write!(f, "{},{}", self.latitude, self.longitude)?;
   158→        }
   159→        if let Some(ts) = self.updated_at {
   160→            let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
   161→                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
   162→                .unwrap_or_default()
   163→                .as_secs() as i64;
   164→            let age_secs = now.saturating_sub(ts);
   165→            let age_str = if age_secs < 60 {
   166→                "just now".to_string()
   167→            } else if age_secs < 3600 {
   168→                format!("{}m ago", age_secs / 60)
   169→            } else if age_secs < 86400 {
   170→                format!("{}h ago", age_secs / 3600)
   171→            } else {
   172→                format!("{}d ago", age_secs / 86400)
   173→            };
   174→            write!(f, " (updated {age_str})")?;
   175→        }
   176→        Ok(())
   177→    }
   178→}

   253→    ///

   255→    /// (`[providers.<name>.models.<id>]`) take precedence over these.
   256→    ///

   260→    /// ```
   261→    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "HashMap::is_empty")]
   262→    pub models: HashMap<String, ModelOverride>,
   263→    /// Upstream HTTP/SOCKS proxy for all outbound requests.
   264→    ///
   265→    /// Supports `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://`, and `socks5h://` schemes.
   266→    /// Proxy authentication via URL: `http://user:pass@host:port`.
   267→    /// When set, overrides the `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` environment
   268→    /// variables for all traffic (providers, channels, tools, OAuth).
   269→    /// Localhost/loopback addresses are automatically excluded (`no_proxy`).
   270→    #[serde(
   271→        default,
   272→        skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none",
   273→        serialize_with = "crate::schema::serialize_option_secret",
   274→        deserialize_with = "crate::schema::deserialize_option_secret"

   285→    /// Returns `true` when both the agent name and user name have been set
   286→    /// (i.e. the onboarding wizard has been completed).
   287→    pub fn is_onboarded(&self) -> bool {
   288→        self.identity.name.is_some() && self.user.name.is_some()
   289→    }

   291→
   292→fn serialize_option_secret<S: serde::Serializer>(
   293→    secret: &Option<Secret<String>>,
   294→    serializer: S,
   295→) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
   296→    match secret {
   297→        Some(s) => serializer.serialize_some(s.expose_secret()),
   298→        None => serializer.serialize_none(),
   299→    }
   300→}
   301→
   302→fn deserialize_option_secret<'de, D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Option<Secret<String>>, D::Error>
   303→where
   304→    D: Deserializer<'de>,
   305→{
   306→    let opt: Option<String> = Option::deserialize(deserializer)?;
   307→    Ok(opt.map(Secret::new))
   308→}
   309→
   310→fn default_true() -> bool {
   311→    true
   312→}
   313→
   314→const fn is_true(value: &bool) -> bool {
   315→    *value
   316→}
   317→
   318→const fn is_false(value: &bool) -> bool {
   319→    !*value
   320→}
   321→
   322→const fn is_default_provider_stream_transport(value: &ProviderStreamTransport) -> bool {
   323→    matches!(value, ProviderStreamTransport::Sse)
   324→}
   325→
   326→const fn is_default_wire_api(value: &WireApi) -> bool {
   327→    matches!(value, WireApi::ChatCompletions)
   328→}

     1→//! Configuration validation engine.
     2→//!
     3→//! Validates TOML configuration files against the known schema, detects
     4→//! unknown/misspelled fields, and reports security warnings.
     5→
     6→use std::path::Path;
     7→
     8→use crate::schema::MoltisConfig;
     9→
    10→#[path = "validate/schema_map.rs"]
    11→mod schema_map;
    12→#[path = "validate/semantic.rs"]
    13→mod semantic;
    14→
    15→/// Severity level for a diagnostic.
    16→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
    17→pub enum Severity {
    18→    Error,
    19→    Warning,
    20→    Info,
    21→}
    22→
    23→impl std::fmt::Display for Severity {
    24→    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
    25→        match self {
    26→            Self::Error => write!(f, "error"),
    27→            Self::Warning => write!(f, "warning"),
    28→            Self::Info => write!(f, "info"),
    29→        }
    30→    }
    31→}
    32→
    33→/// A single validation diagnostic.
    34→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    35→pub struct Diagnostic {
    36→    pub severity: Severity,
    37→    /// Category: "syntax", "unknown-field", "deprecated-field", "unknown-provider", "type-error",
    38→    /// "security", "file-ref"
    39→    pub category: &'static str,
    40→    /// Dotted path, e.g. "server.bnd"
    41→    pub path: String,
    42→    pub message: String,
    43→}
    44→
    45→/// Result of validating a configuration file.
    46→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    47→pub struct ValidationResult {
    48→    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,
    49→    pub config_path: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    50→}
    51→
    52→impl ValidationResult {
    53→    /// Returns `true` if any diagnostic is an error.
    54→    #[must_use]
    55→    pub fn has_errors(&self) -> bool {
    56→        self.diagnostics
    57→            .iter()
    58→            .any(|d| d.severity == Severity::Error)
    59→    }
    60→
    61→    /// Count diagnostics by severity.
    62→    #[must_use]
    63→    pub fn count(&self, severity: Severity) -> usize {
    64→        self.diagnostics
    65→            .iter()
    66→            .filter(|d| d.severity == severity)
    67→            .count()
    68→    }
    69→}
    70→
    71→pub fn validate(path: Option<&Path>) -> ValidationResult {
    72→    let config_path = if let Some(p) = path {
    73→        Some(p.to_path_buf())
    74→    } else {
    75→        crate::loader::find_config_file()
    76→    };
    77→
    78→    let Some(ref actual_path) = config_path else {
    79→        return ValidationResult {
    80→            diagnostics: vec![Diagnostic {
    81→                severity: Severity::Info,
    82→                category: "file-ref",
    83→                path: String::new(),
    84→                message: "no config file found; using defaults".into(),
    85→            }],
    86→            config_path: None,
    87→        };
    88→    };
    89→
    90→    match std::fs::read_to_string(actual_path) {
    91→        Ok(content) => {
    92→            let mut result = validate_toml_str(&content);
    93→            result.config_path = Some(actual_path.clone());
    94→            semantic::check_file_references(&content, actual_path, &mut result.diagnostics);
    95→            result
    96→        },
    97→        Err(e) => ValidationResult {
    98→            diagnostics: vec![Diagnostic {
    99→                severity: Severity::Error,
   100→                category: "syntax",
   101→                path: String::new(),
   102→                message: format!("failed to read config file: {e}"),
   103→            }],
   104→            config_path: Some(actual_path.clone()),
   105→        },
   106→    }
   107→}
   108→
   109→/// Validate a TOML string without file-system side effects (useful for tests
   110→/// and the gateway).
   111→#[must_use]
   112→pub fn validate_toml_str(toml_str: &str) -> ValidationResult {
   113→    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
   114→
   115→    // 1. Syntax - parse raw TOML
   116→    let toml_value: toml::Value = match toml::from_str(toml_str) {
   117→        Ok(v) => v,
   118→        Err(e) => {
   119→            diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
   120→                severity: Severity::Error,
   121→                category: "syntax",
   122→                path: String::new(),
   123→                message: format!("TOML syntax error: {e}"),
   124→            });
   125→            return ValidationResult {
   126→                diagnostics,
   127→                config_path: None,
   128→            };
   129→        },
   130→    };
   131→
   132→    // 2. Unknown fields - walk the TOML tree against KnownKeys
   133→    let schema = schema_map::build_schema_map();
   134→    schema_map::check_unknown_fields(&toml_value, &schema, "", &mut diagnostics);
   135→
   136→    // 3. Deprecation warnings on raw TOML keys
   137→    let conflicting_replacements = semantic::check_deprecated_fields(&toml_value, &mut diagnostics);
   138→
   139→    // 4. Provider name hints
   140→    if let Some(providers) = toml_value.get("providers").and_then(|v| v.as_table()) {
   141→        semantic::check_provider_names(providers, &mut diagnostics);
   142→    }
   143→
   144→    // 5. Type check - attempt full deserialization
   145→    if let Err(e) = toml::from_str::<MoltisConfig>(toml_str) {
   146→        let message = format!("type error: {e}");
   147→        if !semantic::should_suppress_deprecated_conflict_type_error(
   148→            &message,
   149→            &conflicting_replacements,
   150→        ) {
   151→            diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
   152→                severity: Severity::Error,
   153→                category: "type-error",
   154→                path: String::new(),
   155→                message,
   156→            });
   157→        }
   158→    }
   159→
   160→    // 6. Semantic warnings on parsed config (only if it parses)
   161→    if let Ok(config) = toml::from_str::<MoltisConfig>(toml_str) {
   162→        semantic::check_semantic_warnings(&config, &mut diagnostics);
   163→    }
   164→
   165→    ValidationResult {
   166→        diagnostics,
   167→        config_path: None,
   168→    }
   169→}
   170→
   171→fn levenshtein(a: &str, b: &str) -> usize {
   172→    let a_bytes = a.as_bytes();
   173→    let b_bytes = b.as_bytes();
   174→    let n = a_bytes.len();
   175→    let m = b_bytes.len();
   176→    if n == 0 {
   177→        return m;
   178→    }
   179→    if m == 0 {
   180→        return n;
   181→    }
   182→
   183→    let mut prev: Vec<usize> = (0..=m).collect();
   184→    let mut curr = vec![0; m + 1];
   185→    for (i, &ac) in a_bytes.iter().enumerate() {
   186→        curr[0] = i + 1;
   187→        for (j, &bc) in b_bytes.iter().enumerate() {
   188→            let cost = if ac == bc {
   189→                0
   190→            } else {
   191→                1
   192→            };
   193→            let del = prev[j + 1] + 1;
   194→            let ins = curr[j] + 1;
   195→            let sub = prev[j] + cost;
   196→            curr[j + 1] = del.min(ins).min(sub);
   197→        }
   198→        std::mem::swap(&mut prev, &mut curr);
   199→    }
   200→    prev[m]
   201→}
   202→
   203→fn suggest<'a>(needle: &str, candidates: &[&'a str], max_distance: usize) -> Option<&'a str> {
   204→    let mut best: Option<(&'a str, usize)> = None;
   205→    for &candidate in candidates {
   206→        let dist = levenshtein(needle, candidate);
   207→        if dist <= max_distance {
   208→            match best {
   209→                Some((_, best_dist)) if dist < best_dist => best = Some((candidate, dist)),
   210→                None => best = Some((candidate, dist)),
   211→                _ => {},
   212→            }
   213→        }
   214→    }
   215→    best.map(|(candidate, _)| candidate)
   216→}

   221→mod tests;
