   210→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   211→# MODEL OVERRIDES (GLOBAL)
   212→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   213→# Override context window sizes for specific models across all providers.
   214→# Provider-scoped overrides ([providers.<name>.model_overrides.<id>]) take precedence.
   215→#
   216→# [models.claude-opus-4-6]
   217→# context_window = 1_000_000                  # Override the built-in heuristic
   218→#
   219→# [models.glm-5-turbo]
   220→# context_window = 200_000
   221→
   222→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   223→# CHAT SETTINGS
   224→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   225→
   226→[chat]
   227→message_queue_mode = "followup"   # Default: process queued messages one-by-one after the current run.
   228→                                  # How to handle messages during an active agent run:
   229→                                  #   "followup" - Queue messages, replay one-by-one after run
   230→                                  #   "collect"  - Buffer messages, concatenate as single message
   231→# prompt_memory_mode = "live-reload"  # How MEMORY.md reaches the prompt:
   232→                                      #   "live-reload"            - Re-read MEMORY.md before each turn
   233→                                      #   "frozen-at-session-start" - Freeze the first MEMORY.md snapshot per session
   234→# workspace_file_max_chars = 32000  # Optional: per-file prompt cap for AGENTS.md / TOOLS.md before truncation.
   235→# priority_models = ["claude-opus-4-5", "gpt-5.2", "gemini-3-flash"]  # Optional: models to pin first in selectors
   236→# allowed_models = ["gpt 5.2"]  # Legacy field (currently ignored).
   237→
   238→# ── Compaction ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   239→# Strategy used to shrink a session when its context window fills up, or when
   240→# a user invokes `/compact`. Four modes are available — pick the one that
   241→# matches your cost/fidelity trade-off. See docs/src/compaction.md for a full
   242→# comparison table and picking guide.
   243→#
   244→# Modes:
   245→#   "deterministic"        (default) Zero LLM calls. Replaces the entire
   246→#                          history with a single extracted summary message
   247→#                          (counts, tool names, file paths, recent user
   248→#                          requests, head+tail timeline). Fast, free, offline,
   249→#                          low fidelity. Best for short chat channels and
   250→#                          cost-sensitive deployments.
   251→#
   252→#   "recency_preserving"   Zero LLM calls. Keeps head (system prompt +
   253→#                          first exchange) and recent tail verbatim (sized
   254→#                          by token budget). Collapses the middle into a
   255→#                          short marker message and replaces any bulky
   256→#                          tool-result content in the retained slice with a
   257→#                          placeholder. Repairs orphaned tool_use /
   258→#                          tool_result pairs so strict providers accept the
   259→#                          retry. Mid fidelity, free.
   260→#
   261→#   "structured"           Head + LLM structured summary + tail. Same
   262→#                          boundary logic as recency_preserving, but the
   263→#                          middle is summarised with a single LLM call
   264→#                          using a Goal / Progress / Decisions / Files /
   265→#                          Next Steps template (same convention as
   266→#                          hermes-agent and openclaw safeguard). Iterative
   267→#                          re-compaction preserves prior summary sections.
   268→#                          Highest fidelity, costs a summary LLM call per
   269→#                          compaction. Falls back to recency_preserving on
   270→#                          LLM failure or empty summary.
   271→#
   272→#   "llm_replace"          Replaces the entire history with a single
   273→#                          LLM-generated summary. Pre-PR-#653 behaviour.
   274→#                          Best for maximum token reduction when the session
   275→#                          provider is cheap and the tail isn't worth
   276→#                          preserving.
   277→#
   278→[chat.compaction]
   279→mode = "deterministic"              # "deterministic" | "recency_preserving" | "structured" | "llm_replace"
   280→# threshold_percent = 0.95          # Fires auto-compaction when the next request is estimated to exceed
   281→                                    # this fraction of the model context window. Also multiplied into
   282→                                    # the verbatim tail budget for recency_preserving / structured modes.
   283→                                    # Default matches the pre-PR-#653 hardcoded trigger so upgrades are
   284→                                    # behaviour-neutral. Range: 0.10–0.95. Lower = more aggressive compaction.
   285→# protect_head = 3                  # Number of leading messages kept verbatim by recency/structured modes.
   286→# protect_tail_min = 20             # Floor for tail messages kept verbatim (recency/structured modes).
   287→# tail_budget_ratio = 0.20          # Size of the verbatim tail as a fraction of threshold_percent × context_window.
   288→                                    # Example (defaults): 200K context × 0.95 × 0.20 = 38K tokens of tail preserved.
   289→# tool_prune_char_threshold = 200   # Tool-result content longer than this is replaced with a placeholder
   290→                                    # when recency/structured modes prune the middle region.
   291→# summary_model = "openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-flash"  # RESERVED — auxiliary-model subsystem not yet wired
   292→                                                         # (tracked by beads issue moltis-8me). Setting this
   293→                                                         # today emits a one-shot runtime WARN and has no
   294→                                                         # effect on the structured / llm_replace strategies,
   295→                                                         # which still use the session's primary provider.
   296→# max_summary_tokens = 4096         # RESERVED — see summary_model above. Default is 4096 but the value
   297→                                    # is not yet applied to the streaming summary call.
   298→# show_settings_hint = true         # Append "Change chat.compaction.mode in moltis.toml…" to every
   299→                                    # compaction notice (web UI card + channel messages). Default: true.
   300→                                    # Set to false once you know the setting exists to hide the repetitive
   301→                                    # footer without losing the mode + token metadata.
   302→
   303→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   304→# SUB-AGENT SPAWN PRESETS (OPTIONAL)
   305→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   306→# Configure reusable presets for sub-agents spawned via the `spawn_agent` tool.
   307→#
   308→# ⚠️  SCOPE: `[agents.presets.*]` applies ONLY to sub-agents spawned via the
   309→# `spawn_agent` tool. The `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` fields under a preset
   310→# do NOT filter tools for the main agent session. To allow/deny tools for the
   311→# main session, use the `[tools.policy]` section further down this file.
   312→# `[agents] default_preset` likewise only selects the sub-agent preset used
   313→# when `spawn_agent.preset` is omitted — it does not apply to the main session.
   314→#
   315→# [agents]
   316→# default_preset = "research"      # Sub-agent preset used when spawn_agent.preset is omitted
   317→#
   318→# [agents.presets.research]
   319→# model = "openai/gpt-5.2"
   320→# allow_tools = ["web_search", "web_fetch", "sessions_send", "task_list"]
   321→# deny_tools = ["exec"]
   322→# delegate_only = false
   323→# system_prompt_suffix = "Focus on gathering and summarizing evidence."
   324→
   325→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   326→# TOOLS
   327→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   328→
   329→[tools]
   330→agent_timeout_secs = 600          # Max seconds for an agent run (0 = no timeout)
   331→agent_max_iterations = 25         # Max LLM/tool loop iterations before stopping
   332→agent_max_auto_continues = 2      # Auto-continue nudges when model stops mid-task (0 = off)
   333→agent_auto_continue_min_tool_calls = 3  # Min tool calls before auto-continue can trigger
   334→max_tool_result_bytes = 50000     # Max bytes per tool result before truncation (50KB)
   335→# registry_mode = "full"          # "full" = all schemas every turn, "lazy" = tool_search discovery
   336→agent_loop_detector_window = 3    # Fire intervention after N identical failing tool calls in a row (0 = disable)
   337→agent_loop_detector_strip_tools_on_second_fire = true  # On second consecutive fire, strip tool schemas for one turn to force a text response
   338→tool_result_compaction_ratio = 75     # % of context_window before oldest tool results are compacted (0 = disable)
   339→preemptive_overflow_ratio = 90        # % of context_window before hard ContextWindowExceeded error
   340→compaction_min_iterations = 3         # Min loop iterations before per-iteration compaction can fire
   341→
   342→# ── Maps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   343→
   344→[tools.maps]
   345→provider = "google_maps"          # Map provider used by show_map:
   346→                                  #   "google_maps" (default)
   347→                                  #   "apple_maps"
   348→                                  #   "openstreetmap"
   349→
   350→# ── Native filesystem tools (Read/Write/Edit/MultiEdit/Glob/Grep) ─────────────
   351→# All fields are optional. Defaults are conservative — the fs tools work
   352→# out of the box with no configuration.
   353→
   354→[tools.fs]
   355→# workspace_root = "/home/user/projects/my-app"
   356→                                  # Absolute path used as the default search root
   357→                                  # for Glob/Grep when the LLM call omits `path`.
   358→                                  # Unset → calls without an explicit `path` are
   359→                                  # rejected with a clear error.
   360→allow_paths = []                  # Absolute path globs the fs tools are allowed
   361→                                  # to access. Empty = no allowlist (all paths OK).
   362→                                  # Evaluated after canonicalization so symlinks
   363→                                  # can't escape the list.
   364→                                  # Example: ["/data/home/*", "/srv/workspace/**"]
   365→deny_paths = []                   # Absolute path globs the fs tools must refuse.
   366→                                  # Deny wins over allow. Also evaluated after
   367→                                  # canonicalization. Example:
   368→                                  #   ["/data/secrets/**", "**/.env*", "/etc/**"]
   369→track_reads = false               # Record per-session Read history for loop
   370→                                  # detection and the must_read_before_write
   371→                                  # invariant. Cheap in-memory map keyed by
   372→                                  # session_key.
   373→must_read_before_write = false    # Refuse Write/Edit/MultiEdit calls targeting
   374→                                  # files the session has not previously Read.
   375→                                  # Requires track_reads = true. Returns a typed
   376→                                  # must_read_before_write payload the LLM can
   377→                                  # branch on.
   378→require_approval = true           # When true, Write/Edit/MultiEdit pause for
   379→                                  # explicit operator approval before mutating.
   380→                                  # Uses the existing approval queue and will
   381→                                  # time out if nobody approves the request.
   382→max_read_bytes = 10485760         # Maximum bytes a single Read can return before
   383→                                  # the file is rejected with a typed "too_large"
   384→                                  # payload (10 MB).
   385→binary_policy = "reject"          # How to handle binary files in Read:
   386→                                  #   "reject" — return typed binary marker (default)
   387→                                  #   "base64" — return base64-encoded bytes in the
   388→                                  #              payload (still capped by max_read_bytes)
   389→respect_gitignore = true          # When true (default), Glob and Grep skip files
   390→                                  # ignored by .gitignore / .ignore / .git/info/exclude
   391→                                  # while walking. Set false to include ignored files.
   392→checkpoint_before_mutation = false  # When true, Write/Edit/MultiEdit call the
   393→                                  # existing CheckpointManager to snapshot the target
   394→                                  # file before mutating, so the LLM (or operator) can
   395→                                  # restore it later via `checkpoint_restore`. Default
   396→                                  # off because checkpoints grow with activity and
   397→                                  # size scales with file size.
   398→# context_window_tokens = 200000    # Model context window in tokens. When set, Read's
   399→                                  # per-call byte cap scales adaptively so a single
   400→                                  # Read uses at most ~20% of the model's working set
   401→                                  # (clamped to [50 KB, 512 KB]). Unset → fixed 256 KB.
   402→                                  # Typical values: 200000 for Claude Sonnet, 1000000
   403→                                  # for Claude Opus 4.6 1M, 128000 for GPT-4 Turbo.
   404→
   405→# ── Command Execution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   406→
   407→[tools.exec]
   408→default_timeout_secs = 30         # Default timeout for commands
   409→max_output_bytes = 204800         # Max command output bytes (200KB)
   410→approval_mode = "on-miss"         # When to require approval:
   411→                                  #   "always"  - Always ask before running
   412→                                  #   "on-miss" - Ask if not in allowlist
   413→                                  #   "never"   - Never ask (for headless deployments)
   414→security_level = "allowlist"      # Security mode:
   415→                                  #   "permissive" - Allow most commands
   416→                                  #   "allowlist"  - Only allow listed commands
   417→                                  #   "strict"     - Very restrictive
   418→allowlist = []                    # Command patterns to allow (when security_level = "allowlist").
   419→                                  # With approval_mode = "never", a non-empty allowlist is enforced:
   420→                                  # commands that don't match are denied (safe bins still allowed).
   421→                                  # An empty allowlist in "never" mode is unrestricted.
   422→                                  # Example: ["git *", "npm *", "cargo *"]
   423→host = "local"                    # Where to run commands:
   424→                                  #   "local" - Run on this machine (default)
   425→                                  #   "node"  - Run on a connected Moltis node
   426→                                  #   "ssh"   - Run through the system ssh client
   427→# node = "mac-mini"               # Default node id/display name when host = "node"
   428→# ssh_target = "deploy@box"       # SSH host alias or user@host when host = "ssh"
   429→
   430→# ── Sandbox Configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   431→# Commands run inside isolated containers for security.
   432→
   433→[tools.exec.sandbox]
   434→mode = "all"                      # Which commands to sandbox:
   435→                                  #   "off"      - No sandboxing (commands run on host)
   436→                                  #   "non-main" - Sandbox all except main session
   437→                                  #   "all"      - Sandbox everything (recommended)
   438→scope = "session"                 # Container lifecycle:
   439→                                  #   "command" - New container per command
   440→                                  #   "session" - Container per session (recommended)
   441→                                  #   "global"  - Single shared container
   442→workspace_mount = "ro"            # How to mount workspace in sandbox:
   443→                                  #   "ro"   - Read-only (safe; sandbox commands can read mounted files but cannot modify them)
   444→                                  #   "rw"   - Read-write (can modify files)
   445→                                  #   "none" - No mount
   446→# host_data_dir = "/host/path/data"  # Optional override if auto-detection cannot resolve the host-visible data dir
   447→home_persistence = "shared"       # Persist /home/sandbox across container recreation:
   448→                                  #   "off"     - Ephemeral home
   449→                                  #   "session" - Per-session persisted home
   450→                                  #   "shared"  - One shared persisted home (default)
   451→# shared_home_dir = "/path/to/shared-home"  # Host dir for shared persistence (default: data_dir()/sandbox/home/shared)
   452→backend = "auto"                  # Container backend:
   453→                                  #   "auto"            - Auto-detect (prefers Apple Container on macOS)
   454→                                  #   "docker"          - Use Docker
   455→                                  #   "apple-container" - Use Apple Container (macOS only)
   456→no_network = true                 # Disable network access in sandbox (recommended)
   457→# image = "custom-image:tag"      # Custom Docker image (default: auto-built)
   458→# container_prefix = "moltis"     # Prefix for container names
   459→
   460→# Packages installed in sandbox containers via apt-get.
   461→# This list is used to build the sandbox image. Customize as needed.
   462→packages = [
   463→    # Networking & HTTP
   464→    "curl",
   465→    "wget",
   466→    "ca-certificates",
   467→    "dnsutils",
   468→    "netcat-openbsd",
   469→    "openssh-client",
   470→    "iproute2",
   471→    "net-tools",
   472→    # Language runtimes
   473→    "python3",
   474→    "python3-dev",
   475→    "python3-pip",
   476→    "python3-venv",
   477→    "python-is-python3",
   478→    "nodejs",
   479→    "npm",
   480→    "ruby",
   481→    "ruby-dev",
   482→    "golang-go",
   483→    # Build toolchain & native deps
   484→    "build-essential",
   485→    "clang",
   486→    "libclang-dev",
   487→    "llvm-dev",
   488→    "pkg-config",
   489→    "libssl-dev",
   490→    "libsqlite3-dev",
   491→    "libyaml-dev",
   492→    "liblzma-dev",
   493→    "autoconf",
   494→    "automake",
   495→    "libtool",
   496→    "bison",
   497→    "flex",
   498→    "dpkg-dev",
   499→    "fakeroot",
   500→    # Compression & archiving
   501→    "zip",
   502→    "unzip",
   503→    "bzip2",
   504→    "xz-utils",
   505→    "p7zip-full",
   506→    "tar",
   507→    "zstd",
   508→    "lz4",
   509→    "pigz",
   510→    # Common CLI utilities
   511→    "git",
   512→    "gnupg2",
   513→    "jq",
   514→    "rsync",
   515→    "file",
   516→    "tree",
   517→    "sqlite3",
   518→    "sudo",
   519→    "locales",
   520→    "tzdata",
   521→    "shellcheck",
   522→    "patchelf",
   523→    "tmux",
   524→    # Text processing & search
   525→    "ripgrep",
   526→    # Browser automation dependencies
   527→    "chromium",
   528→    "libxss1",
   529→    "libnss3",
   530→    "libnspr4",
   531→    "libasound2t64",
   532→    "libatk1.0-0t64",
   533→    "libatk-bridge2.0-0t64",
   534→    "libcups2t64",
   535→    "libdrm2",
   536→    "libgbm1",
   537→    "libgtk-3-0t64",
   538→    "libxcomposite1",
   539→    "libxdamage1",
   540→    "libxfixes3",
   541→    "libxrandr2",
   542→    "libxkbcommon0",
   543→    "fonts-liberation",
   544→]
   545→
   546→# Resource limits for sandboxed execution (optional)
   547→[tools.exec.sandbox.resource_limits]
   548→# memory_limit = "512M"           # Memory limit (e.g., "512M", "1G", "2G")
   549→# cpu_quota = 0.5                 # CPU quota as fraction (0.5 = half a core, 2.0 = two cores)
   550→# pids_max = 100                  # Maximum number of processes
   551→
   552→# Tool policy overrides applied when commands run inside the sandbox (layer 6).
   553→# These narrow the effective policy for sandboxed execution only.
   554→# [tools.exec.sandbox.tools_policy]
   555→# allow = ["exec"]                # Only allow exec tool inside sandbox
   556→# deny = ["browser"]              # Deny browser tool inside sandbox
   557→
   558→# ── Tool Policy ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   559→# Control which tools the agent can use. Policies are layered (later wins for
   560→# allow, deny always accumulates across layers):
   561→#
   562→#   1. Global        — this section ([tools.policy])
   563→#   2. Per-provider  — [providers.<name>.policy]
   564→#   3. Per-agent     — [agents.presets.<id>.tools]
   565→#   4. Per-channel   — [channels.<type>.<account>.tools.groups.<chat_type>]
   566→#   5. Per-sender    — [...groups.<chat_type>.by_sender.<sender_id>]
   567→#   6. Sandbox       — [tools.exec.sandbox.tools_policy] (only when sandboxed)
   568→#
   569→# This is the base policy for all sessions. Provider and channel layers
   570→# narrow it further based on runtime context.
   571→
   572→[tools.policy]
   573→allow = []                        # Tools to always allow (e.g., ["exec", "web_fetch"])
   574→deny = []                         # Tools to always deny (e.g., ["browser"])
   575→# profile = "default"             # Named policy profile
   576→
   577→# ── Web Search ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   578→
   579→[tools.web.search]
   580→enabled = true                    # Enable web search tool
   581→provider = "brave"                # Search provider: "brave" or "perplexity"
   582→max_results = 5                   # Number of results to return (1-10)
   583→timeout_seconds = 30              # HTTP request timeout
   584→cache_ttl_minutes = 15            # Cache results for this many minutes (0 = no cache)
   585→duckduckgo_fallback = false       # Off by default; enable only if you want DDG fallback without API keys
   586→# api_key = "..."                 # Brave API key (or set BRAVE_API_KEY env var)
   587→
   588→# Perplexity-specific settings (when provider = "perplexity")
   589→[tools.web.search.perplexity]
   590→# api_key = "..."                 # Or set PERPLEXITY_API_KEY env var
   591→# base_url = "..."                # API base URL (auto-detected from key prefix)
   592→# model = "sonar"                 # Perplexity model to use
   593→
   594→# ── Web Fetch ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   595→
   596→[tools.web.fetch]
   597→enabled = true                    # Enable web fetch tool
   598→max_chars = 50000                 # Max characters to return from fetched content
   599→timeout_seconds = 30              # HTTP request timeout
   600→cache_ttl_minutes = 15            # Cache fetched pages for this many minutes (0 = no cache)
   601→max_redirects = 3                 # Maximum HTTP redirects to follow
   602→readability = true                # Use readability extraction for HTML (cleaner output)
   603→# ssrf_allowlist = ["172.22.0.0/16"] # CIDR ranges exempt from SSRF blocking (e.g. Docker networks)
   604→
   605→# ── Firecrawl (API-based web scraping) ────────────────────────────────────────
   606→# High-quality markdown extraction from web pages, including JS-heavy and
   607→# bot-protected sites.  Used as a standalone firecrawl_scrape tool, as a
   608→# web_search provider, and as a fallback extractor in web_fetch.
   609→# Get an API key at https://firecrawl.dev or self-host.
   610→
   611→# [tools.web.firecrawl]
   612→# enabled = false                        # Enable Firecrawl integration
   613→# api_key = "fc-..."                     # Or set FIRECRAWL_API_KEY env var
   614→# base_url = "https://api.firecrawl.dev" # API endpoint (change for self-hosted)
   615→# only_main_content = true               # Strip navs, footers, sidebars
   616→# timeout_seconds = 30                   # HTTP request timeout
   617→# cache_ttl_minutes = 15                 # Cache scraped pages (0 = no cache)
   618→# web_fetch_fallback = true              # Use as fallback when readability fails
   619→
   620→# ── Browser Automation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   621→# Full browser control via Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
   622→# Use for JavaScript-heavy sites, form filling, screenshots.
   623→
   624→[tools.browser]
   625→enabled = true                    # Enable browser tool
   626→headless = true                   # Run without visible window (true = background)
   627→viewport_width = 2560             # Default viewport width in pixels (QHD for tech users)
   628→viewport_height = 1440            # Default viewport height in pixels
   629→device_scale_factor = 2.0         # HiDPI/Retina scaling (2.0 = Retina, 1.0 = standard)
   630→max_instances = 3                 # Maximum concurrent browser instances
   631→idle_timeout_secs = 300           # Close idle browsers after this many seconds (5 min)
   632→navigation_timeout_ms = 30000     # Page load timeout in milliseconds (30 sec)
   633→sandbox = false                   # Run browser in Docker/Apple Container for isolation
   634→# container_host = "127.0.0.1"   # Host/IP to reach browser container (default: localhost)
   635→                                  # Set to "host.docker.internal" when Moltis runs inside Docker
   636→# browserless_api_version = "v1" # Browserless compatibility mode: "v1" (default) or "v2"
   637→# chrome_path = "/path/to/chrome" # Custom Chrome/Chromium binary path (auto-detected)
   638→# user_agent = "Custom UA"        # Custom user agent string
   639→# chrome_args = []                # Extra Chrome command-line arguments
   640→                                  # Example: ["--disable-extensions", "--disable-gpu"]
   641→
   642→# Domain restrictions for security.
   643→# When set, browser will refuse to navigate to domains not in this list.
   644→# This helps prevent prompt injection from untrusted websites.
   645→allowed_domains = []              # Empty = all domains allowed
   646→# allowed_domains = [
   647→#     "docs.example.com",         # Exact match
   648→#     "*.github.com",             # Wildcard: matches any subdomain of github.com
   649→#     "localhost",                # Allow localhost
   650→#     "127.0.0.1",
   651→# ]
   652→
   653→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   654→# SKILLS
   655→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   656→# Reusable prompt templates and workflows.
   657→
   658→[skills]
   659→enabled = true                    # Enable skills system
   660→search_paths = []                 # Additional directories to search for skills
   661→                                  # Default locations include ~/.moltis/skills/
   662→auto_load = []                    # Skills to always load without explicit activation
   663→                                  # Example: ["code-review", "commit"]
   664→enable_agent_sidecar_files = false # Allow agents to write supplementary text files inside personal skill dirs
   665→
   666→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   667→# MCP SERVERS
   668→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   669→# Model Context Protocol servers provide additional tools and capabilities.
   670→# See https://modelcontextprotocol.io for available servers.
   671→
   672→[mcp]
   673→request_timeout_secs = 30        # Default timeout for MCP requests
   674→# Each server has a name and configuration:
   675→#
   676→# [mcp.servers.server-name]
   677→# command = "npx"                 # Command to run (for stdio transport)
   678→# args = ["-y", "@package/name"]  # Command arguments
   679→# env = {{ KEY = "value" }}         # Environment variables for the process
   680→# enabled = true                  # Whether this server is enabled
   681→# request_timeout_secs = 90       # Optional timeout override for this server
   682→# transport = "stdio"             # Transport: "stdio" (default), "sse", or "streamable-http"
   683→# url = "http://..."              # URL for SSE/Streamable HTTP transport
   684→# headers = {{ Authorization = "Bearer ${{TOKEN}}" }}  # Optional HTTP headers for remote transport
   685→
   686→# Example: Filesystem access
   687→# [mcp.servers.filesystem]
   688→# command = "npx"
   689→# args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/path/to/allow"]
   690→# enabled = true
   691→
   692→# Example: GitHub integration
   693→# [mcp.servers.github]
   694→# command = "npx"
   695→# args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
   696→# env = {{ GITHUB_TOKEN = "${{GITHUB_TOKEN}}" }}
   697→# enabled = true
   698→
   699→# Example: SSE server
   700→# [mcp.servers.remote]
   701→# transport = "sse"
   702→# url = "http://localhost:8080/mcp?api_key=$REMOTE_MCP_KEY"
   703→# headers = {{ "x-api-key" = "${{REMOTE_MCP_KEY}}" }}
   704→# enabled = true
   705→
   706→# Example: Streamable HTTP server
   707→# [mcp.servers.remote-http]
   708→# transport = "streamable-http"
   709→# url = "https://mcp.example.com/mcp"
   710→# headers = {{ Authorization = "Bearer ${{API_KEY}}" }}
   711→# enabled = true
   712→
   713→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   714→# METRICS
   715→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   716→# Prometheus metrics for observability.
   717→
   718→[metrics]
   719→enabled = true                    # Enable metrics collection
   720→prometheus_endpoint = true        # Expose /metrics endpoint for Prometheus scraping
   721→# labels = {{ environment = "production", instance = "main" }}
   722→                                  # Additional labels to add to all metrics
   723→
   724→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   725→# CRON
   726→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   727→# Settings for the cron scheduler.
   728→
   729→# [cron]
   730→# rate_limit_max = 10                # Max jobs created per rate limit window
   731→# rate_limit_window_secs = 60        # Rate limit window in seconds
   732→# session_retention_days = 7         # Auto-clean cron sessions older than N days (0 or omit to disable)
   733→# auto_prune_cron_containers = true  # Auto-remove sandbox containers after cron job completion
   734→
   735→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   736→# HEARTBEAT
   737→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   738→# Periodic health-check agent turns to keep the agent "alive" and responsive.
   739→
   740→[heartbeat]
   741→enabled = true                    # Enable periodic heartbeats
   742→every = "30m"                     # Interval between heartbeats (e.g., "30m", "1h", "6h")
   743→# model = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514"  # Override model for heartbeats
   744→# prompt = "..."                  # Custom heartbeat prompt (default: built-in)
   745→ack_max_chars = 300               # Max characters for acknowledgment reply
   746→deliver = false                   # Deliver heartbeat replies to a channel account
   747→# channel = "my-bot"              # Channel account identifier (required when deliver = true)
   748→# to = "123456789"                # Chat/recipient ID (required when deliver = true)
   749→sandbox_enabled = true            # Run heartbeat commands in sandbox
   750→# sandbox_image = "..."           # Override sandbox image for heartbeats
   751→
   752→# Active hours window - heartbeats only run during this time
   753→[heartbeat.active_hours]
   754→start = "08:00"                   # Start time (HH:MM, 24-hour format)
   755→end = "24:00"                     # End time (HH:MM, "24:00" = end of day)
   756→timezone = "local"                # Timezone: "local" or IANA name like "Europe/Paris"
   757→
   758→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   759→# FAILOVER
   760→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   761→# Automatic fallback to alternative models/providers on failure.
   762→
   763→[failover]
   764→enabled = true                    # Enable automatic failover
   765→fallback_models = []              # Ordered list of fallback models
   766→                                  # Empty = auto-build chain from all registered models
   767→                                  # Example: ["openai/gpt-4o", "anthropic/claude-3-haiku"]
   768→
   769→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   770→# VOICE
   771→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   772→# Voice provider settings for text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-text (STT).
   773→# `providers` controls what appears in the Settings UI provider list.
   774→
   775→[voice.tts]
   776→enabled = true                    # Enable text-to-speech
   777→# provider = "openai"             # Active TTS provider (auto-selects first configured if omitted)
   778→providers = ["openai", "elevenlabs"] # UI allowlist (empty = show all TTS providers)
   779→# All available TTS providers:
   780→#   "openai", "elevenlabs", "google", "piper", "coqui"
   781→
   782→[voice.stt]
   783→enabled = true                    # Enable speech-to-text
   784→# provider = "whisper"            # Active STT provider (auto-selects first configured if omitted)
   785→providers = ["whisper", "mistral", "elevenlabs"] # UI allowlist (empty = show all STT providers)
   786→# All available STT providers:
   787→#   "whisper", "groq", "deepgram", "google", "mistral",
   788→#   "voxtral-local", "whisper-cli", "sherpa-onnx", "elevenlabs-stt"
   789→
   790→# No api_key needed for OpenAI TTS/Whisper when OpenAI is configured as an LLM provider.
   791→# [voice.tts.openai]
   792→# base_url = "https://api.openai.com/v1"     # API endpoint (change for Chatterbox, etc.)
   793→# voice = "alloy"                 # alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer
   794→# model = "tts-1"                 # tts-1 or tts-1-hd
   795→
   796→# [voice.stt.whisper]
   797→# model = "whisper-1"             # default; override when using an OpenAI-compatible proxy
   798→# language = "en"                 # Optional ISO 639-1 hint; omit for auto-detect
   799→
   800→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   801→# NGROK
   802→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   803→# Expose moltis through a public HTTPS tunnel managed by ngrok.
   804→# Requires a build with the `ngrok` feature and an ngrok authtoken.
   805→
   806→[ngrok]
   807→enabled = false                   # true = create a public HTTPS tunnel at startup
   808→# authtoken = "${{NGROK_AUTHTOKEN}}" # Optional if NGROK_AUTHTOKEN env var is already set
   809→# domain = "team-gateway.ngrok.app"  # Optional reserved/static ngrok domain
   810→
   811→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   812→# TAILSCALE
   813→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   814→# Expose moltis via Tailscale Serve (private) or Funnel (public).
   815→
   816→[tailscale]
   817→mode = "off"                      # Tailscale mode:
   818→                                  #   "off"    - Disabled
   819→                                  #   "serve"  - Tailnet-only HTTPS (private)
   820→                                  #   "funnel" - Public HTTPS via Tailscale
   821→reset_on_exit = true              # Reset serve/funnel when gateway shuts down
   822→
   823→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   824→# MEMORY / EMBEDDINGS
   825→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   826→# Configure the embedding provider for memory/RAG features.
   827→
   828→[memory]
   829→# style = "hybrid"               # High-level memory behavior (default = "hybrid"):
   830→                                  #   "hybrid"      - Prompt MEMORY.md + memory_search/memory_get/memory_save
   831→                                  #   "prompt-only" - Prompt MEMORY.md only, no memory tools
   832→                                  #   "search-only" - Memory tools only, no prompt MEMORY.md injection
   833→                                  #   "off"         - Disable prompt memory injection and memory tools
   834→#                                  # Prompt freshness is configured separately in [chat].prompt_memory_mode
   835→# agent_write_mode = "hybrid"    # Where agent-authored memory writes can land (default = "hybrid"):
   836→                                  #   "hybrid"      - Allow MEMORY.md and memory/<name>.md
   837→                                  #   "prompt-only" - Allow MEMORY.md only
   838→                                  #   "search-only" - Allow memory/<name>.md only
   839→                                  #   "off"         - Disable agent-authored memory writes
   840→# user_profile_write_mode = "explicit-and-auto"  # How Moltis writes USER.md (default = "explicit-and-auto"):
   841→                                  #   "explicit-and-auto" - Settings saves plus silent timezone/location capture
   842→                                  #   "explicit-only"     - Settings saves only, no silent timezone/location capture
   843→                                  #   "off"               - Do not write USER.md, keep profile in moltis.toml only
   844→# backend = "builtin"            # Memory backend (default = "builtin"):
   845→                                  #   "builtin" - Built-in SQLite indexer and retriever
   846→                                  #   "qmd"     - External QMD CLI backend
   847→# provider = "auto"               # Embedding provider for the built-in backend (default = auto-detect):
   848→                                  #   "local"   - Built-in local embeddings
   849→                                  #   "ollama"  - Ollama server
   850→                                  #   "openai"  - OpenAI API
   851→                                  #   "custom"  - Custom endpoint
   852→                                  #   (none)    - Auto-detect from available providers
   853→                                  # Ignored while backend = "qmd"
   854→# disable_rag = false             # true => keyword-only search, disables embedding retrieval
   855→# citations = "auto"              # Citation mode (default = "auto"): "on", "off", or "auto"
   856→# llm_reranking = false           # Use the LLM to rerank search results (only meaningful when RAG is enabled)
   857→# search_merge_strategy = "rrf"   # Merge strategy (default = "rrf"): "rrf" or "linear"
   858→# session_export = "on-new-or-reset"  # Session transcript export policy (default = "on-new-or-reset"):
   859→                                  #   "on-new-or-reset" - Export transcripts on /new and /reset
   860→                                  #   "off"             - Disable session transcript export
   861→#                                  # Exported transcripts become searchable memory, not prompt memory
   862→# base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1"  # Builtin backend only: embedding API base (host, /v1, or /embeddings)
   863→# model = "nomic-embed-text"      # Builtin backend only: embedding model name
   864→# api_key = "..."                 # Builtin backend only: API key (optional for local endpoints like Ollama)
   865→
   866→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   867→# CHANNELS
   868→# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   869→# External messaging integrations.
   870→# Note: channels added or edited in the web UI are stored in Moltis's internal
   871→# database at data_dir()/moltis.db. They are not written back into this file.
   872→# Keep channel config here only if you want to manage it manually in TOML.
   873→
   874→[channels]
   875→# Which channel types appear in the web UI's "+ Add Channel" menu.
   876→# Default: ["telegram", "msteams", "discord", "slack", "matrix", "nostr"]
   877→# Add "whatsapp" to enable it in the UI.
   878→# offered = ["telegram", "msteams", "discord", "slack", "matrix", "nostr", "whatsapp"]
   879→
   880→# WhatsApp linked-device accounts
   881→# [channels.whatsapp.my-bot]
   882→# dm_policy = "open"              # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   883→# group_policy = "disabled"       # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   884→# mention_mode = "always"         # "always", "mention", or "none"
   885→# model = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
   886→# model_provider = "anthropic"
   887→# agent_id = "support"            # Default agent for this account
   888→# otp_self_approval = true        # OTP self-approval for non-allowlisted DM users
   889→# otp_cooldown_secs = 300         # Cooldown after 3 failed OTP attempts
   890→# [channels.whatsapp.my-bot.channel_overrides."120363456789@g.us"]
   891→# agent_id = "triage"
   892→# [channels.whatsapp.my-bot.user_overrides."15551234567@s.whatsapp.net"]
   893→# agent_id = "research"
   894→
   895→# Telegram bots
   896→# [channels.telegram.my-bot]
   897→# token = "..."                   # Bot token from @BotFather
   898→# dm_policy = "allowlist"         # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   899→# group_policy = "open"           # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   900→# mention_mode = "mention"        # "mention", "always", or "none"
   901→# allowlist = []                  # Telegram user IDs or usernames (strings)
   902→# group_allowlist = []            # Telegram group/chat IDs (strings)
   903→# reply_to_message = false        # Send responses as Telegram replies
   904→# agent_id = "research"           # Default agent for this bot
   905→# otp_self_approval = true        # OTP self-approval for non-allowlisted DM users
   906→# otp_cooldown_secs = 300         # Cooldown after 3 failed OTP attempts
   907→# stream_mode = "edit_in_place"   # "edit_in_place" or "off"
   908→# edit_throttle_ms = 300          # Min ms between streaming edits
   909→# [channels.telegram.my-bot.channel_overrides."-1001234567890"]
   910→# agent_id = "triage"
   911→# [channels.telegram.my-bot.user_overrides."123456789"]
   912→# agent_id = "research"
   913→#
   914→# Per-channel tool policy (restrict tools by chat type and sender):
   915→# [channels.telegram.my-bot.tools.groups.group]
   916→# deny = ["exec", "browser"]      # Deny dangerous tools in group chats
   917→# [channels.telegram.my-bot.tools.groups.group.by_sender."123456"]
   918→# allow = ["*"]                    # Override: trusted sender gets all tools
   919→# [channels.telegram.my-bot.tools.groups.private]
   920→# allow = []                       # DMs: allow all tools (default)
   921→
   922→# Microsoft Teams bots
   923→# [channels.msteams.my-bot]
   924→# app_id = "..."                  # Azure Bot App ID
   925→# app_password = "..."            # Azure Bot App Password (client secret)
   926→# tenant_id = "botframework.com"  # Azure AD tenant ID (for JWT validation)
   927→# webhook_secret = "..."          # Optional query secret for webhook URL (?secret=...)
   928→# allowlist = []                  # User IDs allowed to DM (empty = all unless dm_policy=allowlist)
   929→# dm_policy = "allowlist"         # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   930→# group_policy = "open"           # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   931→# mention_mode = "mention"        # "mention", "always", or "none"
   932→# stream_mode = "edit_in_place"   # "edit_in_place" or "off"
   933→# edit_throttle_ms = 1500         # Min ms between streaming edits
   934→# text_chunk_limit = 4000         # Max chars per message chunk
   935→# reply_style = "top_level"       # "top_level" or "thread"
   936→# welcome_card = true             # Show welcome card in DMs
   937→# group_welcome_card = false      # Show welcome text in group chats
   938→# bot_name = "Moltis"             # Bot display name for welcome cards
   939→# prompt_starters = []            # Prompt starter buttons on welcome card
   940→# max_retries = 3                 # Max retry attempts for failed sends
   941→# history_limit = 50              # Max messages for thread context (Graph API)
   942→
   943→# Discord bots
   944→# [channels.discord.my-bot]
   945→# token = "..."                   # Bot token from Discord Developer Portal
   946→# dm_policy = "allowlist"         # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   947→# group_policy = "open"           # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   948→# mention_mode = "mention"        # "mention", "always", or "none"
   949→# allowlist = []                  # Discord user IDs allowed to DM
   950→# guild_allowlist = []            # Discord guild/server IDs (empty = all)
   951→# agent_id = "research"           # Default agent for this bot
   952→# reply_to_message = false        # Send responses as Discord replies
   953→# ack_reaction = "👀"             # Emoji reaction while processing (omit to disable)
   954→# activity = "with AI"            # Bot activity status text
   955→# activity_type = "custom"        # "playing", "listening", "watching", "competing", or "custom"
   956→# status = "online"               # "online", "idle", "dnd", or "invisible"
   957→# otp_self_approval = true        # OTP self-approval for non-allowlisted DM users
   958→# otp_cooldown_secs = 300         # Cooldown after 3 failed OTP attempts
   959→
   960→# Slack bots
   961→# [channels.slack.my-bot]
   962→# bot_token = "xoxb-..."          # Bot user OAuth token
   963→# app_token = "xapp-..."          # App-level token for Socket Mode
   964→# connection_mode = "socket_mode" # "socket_mode" or "events_api"
   965→# signing_secret = "..."          # Required for events_api mode
   966→# dm_policy = "allowlist"         # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   967→# group_policy = "open"           # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   968→# mention_mode = "mention"        # "mention", "always", or "none"
   969→# allowlist = []                  # Slack user IDs (strings)
   970→# channel_allowlist = []          # Slack channel IDs (strings)
   971→# stream_mode = "edit_in_place"   # "edit_in_place", "native", or "off"
   972→# edit_throttle_ms = 500          # Min ms between streaming edits
   973→# thread_replies = true           # Reply in threads
   974→
   975→# Matrix bots / appservices using OIDC, access tokens, or password login
   976→# Three authentication modes:
   977→#   oidc         - OAuth 2.0/OIDC via Matrix Authentication Service (MSC3861).
   978→#                  Recommended for modern homeservers (e.g. matrix.org since April 2025).
   979→#                  Authenticates via browser; no password or token needed.
   980→#   password     - UIAA password login. Required for encrypted Matrix chats on
   981→#                  older homeservers. Moltis creates and persists its own device keys.
   982→#   access_token - Reuses an existing Matrix session. Plain traffic only (no E2EE).
   983→# [channels.matrix.my-bot]
   984→# homeserver = "https://matrix.example.com"
   985→# auth_mode = "oidc"              # "oidc", "password", or "access_token" (auto-detected if omitted)
   986→# access_token = "syt_..."        # Required for access_token mode
   987→# password = "..."                # Required for password mode
   988→# user_id = "@bot:example.com"    # Required for password login, auto-detected for token/OIDC auth
   989→# device_id = "MOLTISBOT"         # Optional device ID for session restore
   990→# device_display_name = "Moltis Matrix Bot"  # Optional display name for password logins
   991→# ownership_mode = "moltis_owned" # "moltis_owned" or "user_managed"
   992→# dm_policy = "allowlist"         # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   993→# room_policy = "allowlist"       # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
   994→# mention_mode = "mention"        # "mention", "always", or "none"
   995→# room_allowlist = []             # Matrix room IDs or aliases
   996→# user_allowlist = []             # Matrix user IDs
   997→# auto_join = "always"            # "always", "allowlist", or "off"
   998→# model = "gpt-4.1"
   999→# model_provider = "openai"
  1000→# stream_mode = "edit_in_place"   # "edit_in_place" or "off"
  1001→# edit_throttle_ms = 500          # Min ms between streaming edits
  1002→# stream_min_initial_chars = 30   # Delay first streamed send until this many chars

   690→
   691→// ── Levenshtein distance ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   692→
   693→/// Compute the Levenshtein edit distance between two strings.
   694→fn levenshtein(a: &str, b: &str) -> usize {
   695→    let a_len = a.len();
   696→    let b_len = b.len();
   697→    if a_len == 0 {
   698→        return b_len;
   699→    }
   700→    if b_len == 0 {
   701→        return a_len;
   702→    }
   703→
   704→    let mut prev: Vec<usize> = (0..=b_len).collect();
   705→    let mut curr = vec![0; b_len + 1];
   706→
   707→    for (i, ca) in a.chars().enumerate() {
   708→        curr[0] = i + 1;
   709→        for (j, cb) in b.chars().enumerate() {
   710→            let cost = if ca == cb {
   711→                0
   712→            } else {
   713→                1
   714→            };
   715→            curr[j + 1] = (prev[j] + cost).min(prev[j + 1] + 1).min(curr[j] + 1);
   716→        }
   717→        std::mem::swap(&mut prev, &mut curr);
   718→    }
   719→    prev[b_len]
   720→}
   721→
   722→/// Find the best match for `needle` among `candidates` using Levenshtein
   723→/// distance. Returns `Some(best)` if the distance is <= `max_distance`.
   724→fn suggest<'a>(needle: &str, candidates: &[&'a str], max_distance: usize) -> Option<&'a str> {
   725→    let mut best: Option<(&'a str, usize)> = None;
   726→    for &candidate in candidates {
   727→        let d = levenshtein(needle, candidate);
   728→        if d > 0 && d <= max_distance && best.as_ref().is_none_or(|(_, bd)| d < *bd) {
   729→            best = Some((candidate, d));
   730→        }
   731→    }
   732→    best.map(|(s, _)| s)
   733→}
   734→
   735→// ── Core validation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   736→
   737→/// Walk the TOML value tree against the schema tree and flag unknown keys.
   738→pub(super) fn check_unknown_fields(
   739→    value: &toml::Value,
   740→    schema: &KnownKeys,
   741→    prefix: &str,
   742→    diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
   743→) {
   744→    match (value, schema) {
   745→        (toml::Value::Table(table), KnownKeys::Struct(fields)) => {
   746→            let known_keys: Vec<&str> = fields.keys().copied().collect();
   747→            for (key, child_value) in table {
   748→                let path = if prefix.is_empty() {
   749→                    key.clone()
   750→                } else {
   751→                    format!("{prefix}.{key}")
   752→                };
   753→                if let Some(child_schema) = fields.get(key.as_str()) {
   754→                    check_unknown_fields(child_value, child_schema, &path, diagnostics);
   755→                } else {
   756→                    let level = if prefix.is_empty() {
   757→                        "at top level "
   758→                    } else {
   759→                        ""
   760→                    };
   761→                    let suggestion = suggest(key, &known_keys, 3);
   762→                    let msg = if let Some(s) = suggestion {
   763→                        format!("unknown field {level}(did you mean \"{s}\"?)")
   764→                    } else {
   765→                        format!("unknown field {level}")
   766→                    };
   767→                    diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
   768→                        severity: Severity::Error,
   769→                        category: "unknown-field",
   770→                        path,
   771→                        message: msg.trim().to_string(),
   772→                    });
   773→                }
   774→            }
   775→        },
   776→        (toml::Value::Table(table), KnownKeys::Map(value_schema)) => {
   777→            for (key, child_value) in table {
   778→                let path = if prefix.is_empty() {
   779→                    key.clone()
   780→                } else {
   781→                    format!("{prefix}.{key}")
   782→                };
   783→                check_unknown_fields(child_value, value_schema, &path, diagnostics);
   784→            }
   785→        },
   786→        (
   787→            toml::Value::Table(table),
   788→            KnownKeys::MapWithFields {
   789→                value: value_schema,
   790→                fields,
   791→            },
   792→        ) => {
   793→            for (key, child_value) in table {
   794→                let path = if prefix.is_empty() {
   795→                    key.clone()
   796→                } else {
   797→                    format!("{prefix}.{key}")
   798→                };
   799→                if let Some(child_schema) = fields.get(key.as_str()) {
   800→                    check_unknown_fields(child_value, child_schema, &path, diagnostics);
   801→                } else {
   802→                    check_unknown_fields(child_value, value_schema, &path, diagnostics);
   803→                }
   804→            }
   805→        },
   806→        (toml::Value::Array(arr), KnownKeys::Array(item_schema)) => {
   807→            for (i, item) in arr.iter().enumerate() {
   808→                let path = format!("{prefix}[{i}]");
   809→                check_unknown_fields(item, item_schema, &path, diagnostics);
   810→            }
   811→        },
   812→        // Leaf or type mismatch — stop recursion (type errors caught later)
   813→        _ => {},
   814→    }
   815→}
   816→

    23→pub(super) fn check_deprecated_fields(
    24→    toml_value: &toml::Value,
    25→    diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
    26→) -> Vec<&'static str> {
    27→    let Some(memory) = toml_value.get("memory").and_then(|value| value.as_table()) else {
    28→        return Vec::new();
    29→    };
    30→
    31→    let mut conflicting_replacements = Vec::new();
    32→    if check_deprecated_memory_field(memory, "embedding_provider", "provider", diagnostics) {
    33→        conflicting_replacements.push("provider");
    34→    }
    35→    if check_deprecated_memory_field(memory, "embedding_base_url", "base_url", diagnostics) {
    36→        conflicting_replacements.push("base_url");
    37→    }
    38→    if check_deprecated_memory_field(memory, "embedding_model", "model", diagnostics) {
    39→        conflicting_replacements.push("model");
    40→    }
    41→    if check_deprecated_memory_field(memory, "embedding_api_key", "api_key", diagnostics) {
    42→        conflicting_replacements.push("api_key");
    43→    }
    44→    check_deprecated_ignored_memory_field(
    45→        memory,
    46→        "embedding_dimensions",
    47→        "deprecated field; ignored because embedding dimensions are determined by the provider response",
    48→        diagnostics,
    49→    );
    50→    conflicting_replacements
    51→}

    53→pub(super) fn should_suppress_deprecated_conflict_type_error(
    54→    message: &str,
    55→    conflicting_replacements: &[&str],
    56→) -> bool {
    57→    conflicting_replacements
    58→        .iter()
    59→        .any(|replacement| message.contains(&format!("duplicate field `{replacement}`")))

    62→fn check_deprecated_memory_field(
    63→    memory: &toml::map::Map<String, toml::Value>,
    64→    legacy: &str,
    65→    replacement: &str,
    66→    diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
    67→) -> bool {
    68→    if !memory.contains_key(legacy) {
    69→        return false;
    70→    }
    71→
    72→    if memory.contains_key(replacement) {
    73→        diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
    74→            severity: Severity::Error,
    75→            category: "deprecated-field",
    76→            path: format!("memory.{legacy}"),
    77→            message: format!(
    78→                "deprecated field conflicts with \"memory.{replacement}\"; remove \"memory.{legacy}\""
    79→            ),
    80→        });
    81→        return true;
    82→    }
    83→
    84→    diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
    85→        severity: Severity::Warning,
    86→        category: "deprecated-field",
    87→        path: format!("memory.{legacy}"),
    88→        message: format!("deprecated field; use \"memory.{replacement}\" instead"),
    89→    });
    90→    false
    91→}

   109→/// Check provider names under `[providers]` and warn about unknown ones.
   110→pub(super) fn check_provider_names(
   111→    providers: &toml::map::Map<String, toml::Value>,
   112→    diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
   113→) {
   114→    for name in providers.keys() {
   115→        if PROVIDERS_META_KEYS.contains(&name.as_str()) {
   116→            continue;
   117→        }
   118→        // Custom providers (user-added OpenAI-compatible endpoints) are valid.
   119→        if name.starts_with("custom-") {
   120→            continue;
   121→        }
   122→        if !KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES.contains(&name.as_str()) {
   123→            let suggestion = suggest(name, KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES, 3);
   124→            let msg = if let Some(s) = suggestion {
   125→                format!("unknown provider name (did you mean \"{s}\"?)")
   126→            } else {
   127→                "unknown provider name (custom providers are valid, but check for typos)".into()
   128→            };
   129→            diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
   130→                severity: Severity::Warning,
   131→                category: "unknown-provider",
   132→                path: format!("providers.{name}"),
   133→                message: msg,
   134→            });
   135→        }
   136→    }
   137→}

   817→    // tools: overflow_ratio must be greater than compaction_ratio
   818→    if config.tools.tool_result_compaction_ratio > 0

   827→                config.tools.preemptive_overflow_ratio, config.tools.tool_result_compaction_ratio
   828→            ),

   833→/// Validate a `context_window` override value (optional field).
   834→fn validate_context_window(value: Option<u32>, path: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
   835→    let Some(cw) = value else {
   836→        return;
   837→    };
   838→    if cw == 0 {
   839→        diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
   840→            severity: Severity::Error,
   841→            category: "invalid-value",
   842→            path: path.into(),
   843→            message: "context_window must be at least 1".into(),
   844→        });
   845→    } else if cw > 10_000_000 {
   846→        diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
   847→            severity: Severity::Warning,
   848→            category: "invalid-value",
   849→            path: path.into(),
   850→            message: format!("context_window is {cw}, which is unusually large (> 10M)"),
   851→        });
   852→    }
   853→}

   855→/// Check that file paths referenced in TLS config exist on disk.
   856→pub(super) fn check_file_references(
   857→    toml_str: &str,
   858→    _config_path: &Path,
   859→    diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
   860→) {
   861→    // Only check if we can parse the config
   862→    let Ok(config) = toml::from_str::<MoltisConfig>(toml_str) else {
   863→        return;
   864→    };
   865→
   866→    let file_refs: &[(&str, &Option<String>)] = &[
   867→        ("tls.cert_path", &config.tls.cert_path),
   868→        ("tls.key_path", &config.tls.key_path),
   869→        ("tls.ca_cert_path", &config.tls.ca_cert_path),
   870→    ];
   871→
   872→    for (path_name, value) in file_refs {
   873→        if let Some(file_path) = value {
   874→            let p = Path::new(file_path);
   875→            if !p.exists() {
   876→                diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
   877→                    severity: Severity::Warning,
   878→                    category: "file-ref",
   879→                    path: (*path_name).into(),
   880→                    message: format!("file not found: {file_path}"),
   881→                });
   882→            }
   883→        }
   884→    }
   885→}

   239→
   240→impl ChannelsConfig {
   241→    /// All named channel fields as `(channel_type, accounts)` pairs.
   242→    ///
   243→    /// This is the single source of truth for the set of named channel types.
   244→    /// Keep in sync with the struct fields.
   245→    fn named_fields(&self) -> [(&str, &HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>); 6] {
   246→        [
   247→            ("telegram", &self.telegram),
   248→            ("whatsapp", &self.whatsapp),
   249→            ("msteams", &self.msteams),
   250→            ("discord", &self.discord),
   251→            ("slack", &self.slack),
   252→            ("nostr", &self.nostr),
   253→        ]
   254→    }
   255→
   256→    /// Iterate all channel configs (named + extra) as `(channel_type, accounts)` pairs.
   257→    pub fn all_channel_configs(&self) -> Vec<(&str, &HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>)> {
   258→        let mut v: Vec<(&str, &HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>)> =
   259→            self.named_fields().into_iter().collect();
   260→        for (ct, accounts) in &self.extra {
   261→            v.push((ct.as_str(), accounts));
   262→        }
   263→        v
   264→    }
   265→
   266→    /// Extract the `tools` sub-object for a specific channel account.
   267→    ///
   268→    /// Channel accounts are stored as `serde_json::Value`, so we deserialize
   269→    /// just the `tools` key on demand.
   270→    pub fn tool_policy_for_account(
   271→        &self,
   272→        channel_type: &str,
   273→        account_id: &str,
   274→    ) -> Option<ChannelToolPolicyOverride> {
   275→        let accounts = self
   276→            .all_channel_configs()
   277→            .into_iter()
   278→            .find(|(ct, _)| *ct == channel_type)
   279→            .map(|(_, accounts)| accounts)?;
   280→        let account_val = accounts.get(account_id)?;
   281→        let tools_val = account_val.get("tools")?;
   282→        serde_json::from_value::<ChannelToolPolicyOverride>(tools_val.clone()).ok()
   283→    }
   284→}

```rust
pub(crate) async fn discover_skills_if_enabled(
    config: &moltis_config::MoltisConfig,
) -> Vec<moltis_skills::types::SkillMetadata> {
    if !config.skills.enabled {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let search_paths = moltis_skills::discover::FsSkillDiscoverer::default_paths();
    let discoverer = moltis_skills::discover::FsSkillDiscoverer::new(search_paths);
    match discoverer.discover().await {
        Ok(skills) => skills,
        Err(e) => {
            warn!("failed to discover skills: {e}");
            Vec::new()
        },
    }
}
```

**Key insight:** The `discover_skills_if_enabled()` function checks `config.skills.enabled`. This is where you would add the `config.skills.enable_self_improvement` check.

.get(\"name\")\n            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::message(\"missing 'name'\"))?;\n        let patches = params\n            .get(\"patches\")\n split_frontmatter_body(&raw);\n\n        // Apply patches sequentially to the body.\n        let mut patched_body = body.to_string();\n        let mut applied = 0usize;\n        for (i, patch) in patches.iter().enumerate() {\n            let find = patch\n                .get(\"find\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .ok_or_else(|| .ok_or_else(|| Error::message(format!(\"patch[{i}]: missing 'replace'\")))?;\n\n            if find.is_empty() {\n                return Err(Error::message(format!(\"patch[{i}]: 'find' must not be empty\")).into());\n            }\n            if !patched_body.contains(find) {\n                return Err(Error::message(format!(\n                    \"patch[{i}]: string not found in skill body: {find:?}\"\n                ))\n                .into());\n            }\n\n            patched_body = patched_body.replacen(find, replace, 1);\n            applied += 1;\n        }\n\n        // Optionally update the frontmatter description.\n        let final_content = if let Some(desc) = new_description {\n            let updated_fm = update_frontmatter_description(frontmatter_block, desc);\n            format!(\"{updated_fm}{patched_body}\")\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{frontmatter_block}{patched_body}\")\n        };\n\n        // Ensure trailing newline.\n        let final_content = if final_content.ends_with('\\n') {\n            final_content\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{final_content}\\n\")\n        };\n\n        let checkpoint = self\n ```
     1→# Skill Self-Extension
     2→
     3→Moltis can create, update, and delete personal skills at runtime through agent
     4→tools, enabling the system to extend its own capabilities during a conversation.
     5→
     6→## Overview
     7→
     8→Three agent tools manage personal skills by default:
     9→
    10→| Tool | Description |
    11→|------|-------------|
    12→| `create_skill` | Write a new `SKILL.md` to `<data_dir>/skills/<name>/` |
    13→| `update_skill` | Overwrite an existing skill's `SKILL.md` |
    14→| `delete_skill` | Remove a skill directory |
    15→
    16→When `skills.enable_agent_sidecar_files = true`, a fourth tool becomes
    17→available:
    18→
    19→| Tool | Description |
    20→|------|-------------|
    21→| `write_skill_files` | Write supplementary UTF-8 text files inside an existing personal skill directory |
    22→
    23→Skills created this way are personal and stored in the configured data
    24→directory's `skills/` folder. They become available on the next message
    25→automatically thanks to the skill watcher.
    26→
    27→Before any built-in skill mutation runs, Moltis creates an automatic
    28→checkpoint. Tool results include a `checkpointId` you can later restore with
    29→`checkpoint_restore`.
    30→
    31→## Skill Watcher
    32→
    33→The skill watcher (`crates/skills/src/watcher.rs`) monitors skill directories
    34→for filesystem changes using debounced notifications. When a `SKILL.md` file is
    35→created, modified, or deleted, the watcher emits a `skills.changed` event via
    36→the WebSocket event bus so the UI can refresh. Supplementary file writes do not
    37→change discovery on their own, so the watcher intentionally stays focused on
    38→`SKILL.md`.
    39→
    40→```admonish tip
    41→The watcher uses debouncing to avoid firing multiple events for rapid
    42→successive edits (e.g. an editor writing a temp file then renaming).
    43→```
    44→
    45→## Creating a Skill
    46→
    47→The agent can create a skill by calling the `create_skill` tool:
    48→
    49→```json
    50→{
    51→  "name": "summarize-pr",
    52→  "content": "# summarize-pr\n\nSummarize a GitHub pull request...",
    53→  "description": "Summarize GitHub PRs with key changes and review notes"
    54→}
    55→```
    56→
    57→This writes `<data_dir>/skills/summarize-pr/SKILL.md` with the provided content.
    58→The skill discoverer picks it up on the next message.
    59→
    60→## Writing Supplementary Files
    61→
    62→When `skills.enable_agent_sidecar_files = true`, the agent can add sidecar
    63→files such as shell scripts, templates, `_meta.json`, or `Dockerfile`:
    64→
    65→```json
    66→{
    67→  "name": "summarize-pr",
    68→  "files": [
    69→    {
    70→      "path": "script.sh",
    71→      "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho summarize\n"
    72→    },
    73→    {
    74→      "path": "templates/prompt.txt",
    75→      "content": "Summarize the pull request with risks first.\n"
    76→    }
    77→  ]
    78→}
    79→```
    80→
    81→Safety rules:
    82→
    83→- only writes inside `<data_dir>/skills/<name>/`
    84→- only relative UTF-8 text files
    85→- rejects `..`, absolute paths, hidden path components, and `SKILL.md`
    86→- rejects symlink escapes and oversized batches
    87→- appends an audit entry to `~/.moltis/logs/security-audit.jsonl`
    88→
    89→## Updating a Skill
    90→
    91→```json
    92→{
    93→  "name": "summarize-pr",
    94→  "content": "# summarize-pr\n\nUpdated instructions..."
    95→}
    96→```
    97→
    98→## Deleting a Skill
    99→
   100→```json
   101→{
   102→  "name": "summarize-pr"
   103→}
   104→```
   105→
   106→This removes the entire `<data_dir>/skills/summarize-pr/` directory, including
   107→any supplementary files written alongside `SKILL.md`.
   108→
   109→Deleted skills can be restored from the returned `checkpointId` with
   110→`checkpoint_restore`, as long as the checkpoint still exists.
   111→
```

This reduces hallucination risk and token cost when\nfixing a few lines:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"name\": \"summarize-pr\",\n  \"patches\": [\n    { \"find\": \"key changes\", \"replace\": \"key changes and risks\" },\n    { \"find\": \"review notes\", \"replace\": \"review action items\" }\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Optional: update the frontmatter description too\"\n}\n```\n\nPatches are applied sequentially. If a `find` string is not found, the tool\nreturns an error and no changes are written.\n\n## Deleting a Skill"

   163→---
   164→
   165→## Part 2: Agentic Memory Lifecycle
   166→
   167→### What Hermes does
   168→
   169→Hermes's `MemoryManager` has lifecycle hooks:
   170→- `on_turn_start(query)` → prefetch relevant memories based on the user's message
   171→- `sync_all(user_content, assistant_content)` → after each turn, extract facts worth remembering
   172→- `on_session_end` → summarize the session's key learnings
   173→- `on_pre_compress` → save important context before compaction discards it
   174→- `queue_prefetch_all()` → background async prefetch for the next turn
   175→
   176→### What Moltis already has
   177→
   178→- `silent_turn.rs` — pre-compaction memory flush (runs an LLM turn to extract memories before compacting). This is equivalent to Hermes's `on_pre_compress`.
   179→- `memory_search` tool — agent can explicitly search memory
   180→- `memory_save` tool — agent can explicitly write memory
   181→- `memory_delete` tool — agent can remove memory entries
   182→- `MemoryWriter` trait — shared by save tool and silent turn
   183→- `MemoryRuntime` trait — search + sync operations
   184→- Hybrid search (FTS5 + vector) — better than Hermes's FTS5-only built-in
   185→
   186→### What's missing
   187→
   188→#### 2.1 Memory prefetch on turn start
   189→
   190→**Files:** `crates/chat/src/service/chat_impl.rs`, `crates/memory/src/runtime.rs`
   191→
   192→Before building the system prompt for each turn, query memory with the user's message as the search query. Inject relevant results into the system prompt as a `<recalled_context>` block.
   193→
   194→```rust
   195→// In the chat service, before calling the agent loop:
   196→if memory_enabled && !user_message.is_empty() {
   197→    let results = memory_runtime.search(&user_message_text, 3).await?;
   198→    if !results.is_empty() {
   199→        let recalled = format_recalled_context(&results);
   200→        system_prompt.push_str(&recalled);
   201→    }
   202→}
   203→```
   204→
   205→**Format:**
   206→```xml
   207→<recalled_context>
   208→The following was recalled from your long-term memory as potentially relevant:
   209→
   210→- [memory/2026-04-15.md] User prefers streaming API calls over batch...
   211→- [MEMORY.md] Project uses Rust workspace with 46+ crates...
   212→</recalled_context>
   213→```
   214→
   215→**Implementation details:**
   216→- Add `prefetch_memory(query: &str, limit: usize) -> Vec<SearchResult>` to `MemoryRuntime`
   217→- Call it in the chat service before prompt assembly
   218→- Gate behind `[memory] enable_prefetch = true` (default true)
   219→- Add config field to schema + validate
   220→- Use a low limit (3-5 results) to avoid prompt bloat
   221→- Skip prefetch for very short messages (< 10 chars) or system commands
   222→
   223→**Tests:**
   224→- Integration test: memory prefetch injects recalled context into prompt
   225→- Test: prefetch skipped when disabled
   226→- Test: prefetch skipped for very short messages
   227→- Test: empty memory returns no `<recalled_context>` block
   228→
   229→#### 2.2 Post-turn memory sync
   230→
   231→**Files:** `crates/chat/src/service/chat_impl.rs`, `crates/agents/src/silent_turn.rs`
   232→
   233→After each turn completes, run a lightweight background extraction. This is different from the pre-compaction flush — it runs after **every** turn, not just before compaction.
   234→
   235→**Design options:**
   236→
   237→**Option A: Background silent turn (heavier, more thorough)**
   238→- After each turn, spawn a background task that runs a mini silent turn
   239→- The mini turn reviews only the latest user message + assistant response (not the full history)
   240→- Writes to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` if it finds anything worth remembering
   241→- Pros: LLM-powered extraction is highest quality
   242→- Cons: doubles LLM cost per turn, adds latency if not truly async
   243→
   244→**Option B: Rule-based extraction (lighter, deterministic)**
   245→- After each turn, run heuristic extraction:
   246→  - If assistant mentioned a user preference → extract it
   247→  - If the turn resolved a technical issue → log the solution
   248→  - If the turn involved >N tool calls → log the workflow summary
   249→- Pros: zero extra LLM cost, instant
   250→- Cons: limited quality, hard to maintain rules
   251→
   252→**Option C: Periodic background flush (compromise)**
   253→- Every N turns (configurable, default 5), run a silent turn that reviews the last N turns
   254→- Between flushes, do nothing
   255→- Pros: amortizes LLM cost, still gets good extraction
   256→- Cons: can miss things if session ends before next flush
   257→
   258→**Recommendation:** Start with **Option C** (periodic flush every N turns). It's the best cost/quality tradeoff:
   259→
   260→```toml
   261→[memory]
   262→# Run a background memory extraction every N turns (0 = disabled, only pre-compaction)
   263→auto_extract_interval = 5
   264→```
   265→
   266→**Implementation:**
   267→- Add turn counter to chat service state
   268→- After each turn, increment counter
   269→- When counter hits threshold, spawn background silent turn with last N messages
   270→- Reset counter
   271→- Also flush on session end (new lifecycle event)
   272→
   273→**Tests:**
   274→- Unit test: counter increments and triggers at threshold
   275→- Unit test: counter resets after flush
   276→- Integration test: memories actually written after N turns
   277→
   278→#### 2.3 Session-end memory summary
   279→
   280→**File:** `crates/chat/src/service/chat_impl.rs`
   281→
   282→When a session ends (user closes chat, explicit `/end`, or timeout), run a final silent turn that:
   283→1. Summarizes what was accomplished
   284→2. Notes any unfinished work
   285→3. Saves to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`
   286→
   287→This ensures no conversation's context is lost, even if compaction never triggers.
   288→
   289→**Implementation:**
   290→- Add a `on_session_end` hook in the chat service
   291→- Reuse the `run_silent_memory_turn` from `silent_turn.rs` with a different system prompt focused on session summarization
   292→- Gate behind `[memory] enable_session_summary = true` (default true)
   293→
   294→**System prompt for session-end:**
   295→```
   296→You are a session summarizer. Review the conversation and write a concise summary to memory.
   297→
   298→Focus on:
   299→- What was accomplished (key outcomes and decisions)
   300→- What was left unfinished (follow-up items)
   301→- Any preferences or patterns the user demonstrated
   302→- Technical context that would help resume this work
   303→
   304→Write to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (append, don't overwrite).
   305→Be concise — 5-15 bullet points maximum.
   306→```

   311→- Test: empty session (no messages) doesn't trigger summary
